docs.title: How to Choose Collectors
docs.text: What a scrape holds is decided three ways: which collector packages are installed, which collectors are enabled, and what each scrape asks for.

docs.title: Install collectors
docs.text:
Install a collector's package, or a group of them:

apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter-wireguard
apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter-network

The service reloads with the new collector. Collectors lists each collector, its package, its groups and what it depends on.

docs.title: Disable a collector
docs.text:
To stop serving a collector that is installed, base collectors included, set enabled to 0 in its section. The section is named after the collector's module: the name with _ for -, as ltq_dsl for ltq-dsl.

uci set prometheus-exporter.softnet=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.softnet.enabled=0
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

A disabled collector is not run, the jail mounts nothing for it, and a scrape that names it in collect[] is refused with a 400. To serve it again, set enabled back to 1, or delete its section if nothing else is set there:

uci delete prometheus-exporter.softnet
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

In LuCI, the switch of its row on the Collectors tab does the same: see How to use the LuCI app.

docs.title: Remove a collector
docs.text: Remove its package: see How to remove the exporter.

docs.title: Choose per scrape
docs.text:
To have one scrape job take some collectors only, give Prometheus the query parameters:

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: openwrt-wifi
    params:
      collect[]: [ wifi, hostapd_stations ]
    static_configs:
      - targets: [ 'router.lan:9100' ]

exclude[] leaves collectors out instead. A name that is not installed, or a disabled one in collect[], makes the scrape fail with a 400. See HTTP endpoint.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
service prometheus-exporter status
service prometheus-exporter check

status counts the collectors served; check lists each, enabled or not.

docs.title: How to Monitor chrony
docs.text:
Two collectors watch the clock when chronyd keeps it:

  • timesync, in the base package, says whether the clock is synchronized, whichever daemon keeps it, busybox ntpd or chronyd: node_timesync_synchronized{daemon="chronyd"}, its stratum, offset and last update.
  • chrony, a package of its own, has chronyd's details, as chrony_exporter names them: its tracking, each source, and its server statistics where it serves time.

Use timesync to alert on a clock that is not synchronized; add chrony for why.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• chrony is installed and runs: chrony (or chrony-nts), its service enabled, /etc/config/chrony holding its servers.
  • The base package is installed.

docs.title: 1. Install the chrony collector
docs.text:
apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter-chrony

The service reloads with it.

docs.title: 2. Check it
docs.text:
service prometheus-exporter check | grep -e chrony -e timesync
wget -qO- 'http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics?collect[]=chrony&collect[]=timesync' | grep -e '^chrony_tracking_stratum' -e '^node_timesync_synchronized'

chrony_tracking_stratum 3
node_timesync_synchronized{daemon="chronyd"} 1

With busybox ntpd running too, timesync writes a series for each, daemon="ntpd" and daemon="chronyd". Only one should keep the clock: turn the system's NTP client off, in LuCI's System → System → Time Synchronization or with uci set system.ntp.enabled=0.

docs.title: Server statistics
docs.text:
chronyd's server statistics, chrony_serverstats_*, are never in a scrape of /metrics. chronyd answers them on its Unix command socket only, and chronyc reaches that socket only by making one of its own beside it, in /var/run/chrony. Writing there is commanding chronyd, which sets the clock, so the exporter's jail does not give it: under procd the collector asks over chronyd's UDP command port, as chronyc falls back to, which answers tracking and sources, and leaves the server statistics out.

Outside the jail they are read where chronyd serves time, an allow section in /etc/config/chrony. To see them on the device:

prometheus-exporter chrony | grep '^chrony_serverstats_'

docs.title: If it fails
docs.text:
check or the log says Cause chrony has nothing to observe: chronyd is disabled chronyd's init script is disabled. Nothing is wrong. chrony: COMMAND_FAILED (chronyc: exit status 1) chronyd is enabled and does not answer: it is stopped, or does not answer on its command port. timesync has nothing to observe: neither ntpd nor chronyd runs No NTP daemon runs. timesync: SOURCE_UNREADABLE (chronyd is enabled and not running) chronyd is enabled at boot, and stopped.

See Collectors and Metrics.

docs.title: How to Set a Collector's Options
docs.text: Some collectors take options of their own: wifi's stations, dhcp_leases' leases, vmstat's fields, diskstats' device_exclude, textfile's directory, unbound's socket. Collectors lists each collector's options with their defaults; service prometheus-exporter check prints each with its help and value.

docs.title: Set an option
docs.text:
A collector's options are in its section of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, named after its module: the collector's name with _ for -.

uci set prometheus-exporter.wifi=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.wifi.stations=0
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

The section's type must be collector. Without a section, or without the option in it, the collector takes its default.

docs.title: Check the value
docs.text:
service prometheus-exporter check

A value the collector does not take is a FAIL line, as collector wifi, section 'wifi': CONFIG_INVALID (stations: expected a boolean, got "maybe"), and the collector fails in every scrape until it is fixed. check exits 1 then.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Leave out wifi's per-station metrics, which grow with the clients:

uci set prometheus-exporter.wifi=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.wifi.stations=0

Have dhcp_leases write a series per lease, with its address, MAC and hostname:

uci set prometheus-exporter.dhcp_leases=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.dhcp_leases.leases=1

Export more of /proc/vmstat, by a regular expression of its field names:

uci set prometheus-exporter.vmstat=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.vmstat.fields='^(oom_kill|pgpg|pswp|pg.*fault|nr_free_pages).*'

Watch the partitions of an eMMC or SD card too, which diskstats leaves out by default, with flash, loop devices and zram still out:

uci set prometheus-exporter.diskstats=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.diskstats.device_exclude='^(z?ram|loop|mtdblock|ubiblock[0-9]+_)[0-9]+$'

device_exclude is a POSIX extended regular expression, as ucode compiles it; ^$ leaves out no device.

Each is followed by uci commit prometheus-exporter and service prometheus-exporter reload.

docs.title: In LuCI
docs.text:
On Services → Prometheus exporter, Collectors tab, the collector's Edit button opens its options. Save stages them; Save & Apply applies them. See How to use the LuCI app.

For textfile's directory and unbound's socket, which also change what the jail mounts, see How to publish metrics from scripts and How to monitor Unbound.

docs.title: How to Give Programs More Time
docs.text: Some collectors run programs: ethtool, nft, tc, chronyc, mmcli, ubnt-manager. Each such collector's programs get 5 seconds in all per scrape, by default; one still running then is killed, and its collector fails with COMMAND_TIMEOUT. Give them more when a slow device, or a slow radio over ssh, needs it; less, to keep a scrape short.

docs.title: Find the collector that runs out of time
docs.text:
logread -e prometheus-exporter | grep COMMAND_TIMEOUT

daemon.warn prometheus-exporter[1]: collector 'ubnt-manager': COMMAND_TIMEOUT (ubnt-manager: still running after 5 s, killed)

service prometheus-exporter check shows each collector's seconds and where they come from:

  ubnt-manager (Ubiquiti airOS radios): section 'ubnt_manager', enabled
      timeout  5s # the main section's exec_timeout

docs.title: Give one collector more time
docs.text:
Set timeout in its section, named after its module (ubnt_manager for ubnt-manager), from 1 to 30 seconds:

uci set prometheus-exporter.ubnt_manager=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.ubnt_manager.timeout=10
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

In LuCI, the collector's Edit dialog has the same field.

docs.title: Change the default for every collector
docs.text:
Set exec_timeout in the main section, from 1 to 30 seconds. It applies to every collector whose section sets no timeout:

uci set prometheus-exporter.main.exec_timeout=3
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

In LuCI, it is Time for programs on the Exporter tab.

docs.title: Keep within Prometheus's timeout
docs.text:
The collectors run one after the other: a scrape can take as long as the sum of their programs' seconds, and more. Prometheus gives a scrape scrape_timeout, 10 seconds by default, and drops the whole scrape when it runs out. If you raise a collector's seconds near it, raise scrape_timeout for that job too, or scrape that collector in a job of its own:

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: openwrt-radios
    scrape_interval: 60s
    scrape_timeout: 30s
    params:
      collect[]: [ ubnt-manager ]
    static_configs:
      - targets: [ 'router.lan:9100' ]

and leave it out of the main job with exclude[]: [ ubnt-manager ].

The rules of the seconds are in Collector interface, and the options in UCI configuration.

docs.title: How to Compress Scrapes
docs.text: The exporter gzips a scrape when the scraper asks for it, Accept-Encoding: gzip, which Prometheus and vmagent send by default. It is on unless you turned it off.

docs.title: Check that scrapes are compressed
docs.text:
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' http://router.lan:9100/metrics

A compressed reply has Content-Encoding: gzip. service prometheus-exporter status says gzip when asked while it is on.

docs.title: Turn it off
docs.text:
If the scraper's CPU, or the router's, matters more than the bytes on the network:

uci set prometheus-exporter.main.compress=0
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

Scrapes are then plain text, whatever the scraper asks.

docs.title: Turn it back on
docs.text:
uci set prometheus-exporter.main.compress=1
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

docs.title: For one scraper only
docs.text:
Leave compress on, and have the scraper that wants plain text not ask: in Prometheus, enable_compression: false in its scrape config (Prometheus 2.49 and later). A request with Accept-Encoding: gzip;q=0 is answered plain too.

What a compressed scrape saves, and costs, is in Performance on small routers. The rules of the reply are in HTTP endpoint.

docs.title: How to Serve HTTPS with Basic Auth
docs.text: Have every scrape log in with a user and password, over TLS. The exporter takes basic auth over HTTPS only: set the certificate and key with it, or the configuration is refused.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A TLS library for uhttpd: ls /lib/libustream-ssl.so finds it. Without it, install one, as apk add libustream-mbedtls.

  • A certificate and its key, for the name Prometheus reaches the device by. To make a self-signed one for router.lan:

    px5g selfsigned -days 3650 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 \
    -keyout /etc/prometheus-exporter.key -out /etc/prometheus-exporter.crt \
    -subj /CN=router.lan -addext subjectAltName=DNS:router.lan

    uhttpd's own, /etc/uhttpd.crt and /etc/uhttpd.key, also serve, but they name OpenWrt unless uhttpd's config says otherwise, and the certificate is DER: convert it to PEM for Prometheus (openssl x509 -inform der -in uhttpd.crt -out openwrt.crt).

docs.title: 1. Hash the password
docs.text:
Use a long random password, as a scraper's can be. Have the ubus object hash it, so the password is on no command line of the device:

ubus call prometheus-exporter hash_password '{"password":"…"}'

{
    "hash": "$6$rounds=1000$IgztncwtDxRNxtVD$emPK…"
}

To use a hash made elsewhere, it must be $1$ (as uhttpd -m <password> prints), or $5$ or $6$ of at most 2000 rounds, as mkpasswd -m sha-512 -R 1000 makes. openssl passwd -6 makes hashes of 5000 rounds, which are refused. Why: Performance on small routers.

docs.title: 2. Set it
docs.text:
uci set prometheus-exporter.main.auth_user='prometheus'
uci set prometheus-exporter.main.auth_password='$6$rounds=1000$IgztncwtDxRNxtVD$emPK…'
uci set prometheus-exporter.main.cert='/etc/prometheus-exporter.crt'
uci set prometheus-exporter.main.key='/etc/prometheus-exporter.key'
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

Keep the single quotes around the hash: the shell would read its $ otherwise.

If the reload refuses the configuration, logread -e prometheus-exporter says why: a user without a hash, a hash it does not take, or no cert and key.

docs.title: 3. Check it
docs.text:
service prometheus-exporter status

running
listening on https://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics, basic auth, gzip when asked, serving 15 collectors

From the machine that scrapes:

curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://router.lan:9100/metrics
curl -sk -u prometheus:'…' https://router.lan:9100/metrics | head

The first is 401; the second is the scrape.

docs.title: 4. Scrape it
docs.text:
In Prometheus, and in vmagent, which takes the same scrape_configs:

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: openwrt
    scheme: https
    basic_auth:
      username: prometheus
      password_file: /etc/prometheus/openwrt.password
    tls_config:
      ca_file: /etc/prometheus/openwrt.crt   # the router's certificate, self-signed
      server_name: router.lan                # a name the certificate holds
      # insecure_skip_verify: true           # or: no check of the certificate at all
    static_configs:
      - targets: [ 'router.lan:9100' ]

Copy the router's certificate (/etc/prometheus-exporter.crt), not its key, to the Prometheus host as ca_file.

docs.title: Turn it off
docs.text:
uci delete prometheus-exporter.main.auth_user
uci delete prometheus-exporter.main.auth_password
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

With cert and key left, it serves HTTPS without a login; delete them too for HTTP.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• HTTP endpoint: the replies.
  • About the security model: why HTTPS only, and why the handler checks the password itself.
  • In LuCI: the Exporter tab's TLS and basic auth fields hash the password for you. See How to use the LuCI app.

docs.title: How to Install the Exporter
docs.text: Install the base package, then the collectors you want, one by one or in groups. The service starts on its own, on loopback, port 9100.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A device on OpenWrt 25.12, with a shell on it (ssh).
  • The packages: from a package feed your device uses, or as .apk files, which make package builds into bin/ (see Make targets).
  • The device can reach its release's own feeds: the packages depend on uhttpd, ucode modules and rpcd-mod-ucode, which come from there.
  • Neither prometheus-node-exporter-ucode nor prometheus-node-exporter-lua is installed. If one is, see How to move from the feed's exporters instead.

docs.title: 1. Choose the packages
docs.text:
• ucode-prometheus-exporter, the base package: the service and the collectors every device can use.
  • A collector's package, ucode-prometheus-exporter-<name>, for each other collector you want: -wifi, -dnsmasq, -wireguard.
  • Or a group: -network, -wireless, -hardware, or -full for all three and the services every router has.
  • luci-app-prometheus-exporter, for its pages in LuCI.

Collectors lists every collector, its package and its groups.

docs.title: 2. Install them
docs.text:
From a feed:

apk update
apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter ucode-prometheus-exporter-full luci-app-prometheus-exporter

From .apk files, copied to the device's /tmp:

apk update
apk add --allow-untrusted /tmp/ucode-prometheus-exporter-0.1.0-r1.apk \
    /tmp/ucode-prometheus-exporter-wifi-0.1.0-r1.apk \
    /tmp/luci-app-prometheus-exporter-0.1.0-r1.apk

A group's file brings nothing without its collectors' files: install them together. Every package must be of the same version as the base package.

docs.title: 3. Check that it serves
docs.text:
service prometheus-exporter status
wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | head

status says where it listens and how many collectors it serves. For what each collector found, run service prometheus-exporter check.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• How to listen on the LAN, for a Prometheus elsewhere.
  • How to serve HTTPS with basic auth.
  • How to choose collectors.

docs.title: How to Listen on the LAN
docs.text: By default the exporter listens on loopback: only programs on the device reach it. To scrape it from another machine, have it listen on an interface that machine reaches.

docs.title: 1. Choose the interface
docs.text:
Use the name of a logical interface, as /etc/config/network and LuCI name them (lan), not of a device (br-lan). ubus call prometheus-exporter interfaces lists them.

* listens on every address of the device, the WAN's included. Prefer one interface.

docs.title: 2. Set it
docs.text:
uci set prometheus-exporter.main.listen_interface=lan
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

To change the port too, set listen_port.

The service listens on every IPv4 and IPv6 address of the interface. While the interface has no address, it does not start: it logs deferring start until listen interface lan becomes ready and starts once it comes up, and again whenever it goes down and up.

docs.title: 3. Check it
docs.text:
On the device:

service prometheus-exporter status

running
listening on http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics, http://[fd00:ab:cd::1]:9100/metrics, gzip when asked, serving 15 collectors

From the machine that will scrape it:

curl -s http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics | head

docs.title: If it does not answer
docs.text:
• The firewall must accept input on the port from that zone. OpenWrt's default lan zone accepts input; another zone may need a rule:

    uci add firewall rule
uci set firewall.@rule[-1].name='Allow-Prometheus'
uci set firewall.@rule[-1].src='lan'
uci set firewall.@rule[-1].dest_port='9100'
uci set firewall.@rule[-1].proto='tcp'
uci set firewall.@rule[-1].target='ACCEPT'
uci commit firewall
service firewall reload

    Never open it from wan: the metrics name your devices, addresses and clients.

  • status does not say running: the interface has no address yet, and the service waits for it. Check ifstatus lan.

To ask a password of every scrape, and send it over TLS, see How to serve HTTPS with basic auth.

docs.title: How to Use the LuCI App
docs.text: luci-app-prometheus-exporter sets up the exporter and shows how it does, from LuCI.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • luci-app-prometheus-exporter is installed, of the same version as the base package. After installing it, reload LuCI in the browser.

docs.title: Change the exporter's settings
docs.text:
1. Open Services → Prometheus exporter, tab Exporter.
  2. Change the fields. A value the exporter would not take is marked as you type, with why.
  3. Save & Apply.

To serve the LAN, pick its interface in Listen on. For basic auth, fill in TLS certificate and TLS key, then Basic auth user and Basic auth password: the password is hashed on Save, and never shown again. To keep the saved password, leave the field empty; to take basic auth away, empty the user.

docs.title: Switch a collector off or on
docs.text:
1. Open the Collectors tab.
  2. Flip the collector's switch.
  3. Save & Apply.

docs.title: Set a collector's options
docs.text:
1. On the Collectors tab, press Edit on the collector's row. The dialog shows its options, and for a collector that runs programs, the seconds they get; below, the configs it reads and what its jail mounts.
  2. Change the fields, and press Save. The values are staged, not applied: they show among LuCI's unsaved changes.
  3. Save & Apply on the page.

Dismiss drops what the dialog changed.

docs.title: See how the exporter does
docs.text:
Open Status → Prometheus exporter. It shows whether the service is enabled and runs, where it serves /metrics, and runs a scrape on the router to show each collector: OK, Failed with its error, Nothing to observe with why, or Not run when it is switched off. Refresh runs it again.

The scrape runs outside the jail. A collector that is OK here and failing in Prometheus lacks something in the jail: see How to troubleshoot.

docs.title: Let another user in
docs.text: The app's ACL is luci-app-prometheus-exporter. A LuCI user granted it reads and writes /etc/config/prometheus-exporter and calls the exporter's ubus object, and nothing else; read access alone shows the pages without saving. See LuCI app.

docs.title: How to Move from the Feed's Exporters
docs.text: This exporter replaces the packages feed's prometheus-node-exporter-ucode and prometheus-node-exporter-lua. It conflicts with both, takes over their settings when it is installed, and writes other metric names.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• One of the feed's exporters is installed, with its collector packages.
  • The new packages are at hand: see How to install the exporter.

docs.title: 1. Remove the old exporter
docs.text:
apk installs neither feed exporter beside this one, nor this one beside either, and says why:

ERROR: unable to select packages:
  prometheus-node-exporter-ucode-2024.02.07-r2:
    breaks: ucode-prometheus-exporter-0.1.0-r1[!prometheus-node-exporter-ucode>=0]

Remove the old exporter and its collector packages first:

apk del -r prometheus-node-exporter-ucode

or prometheus-node-exporter-lua. apk keeps the old config file if you changed it: that is what the next step reads.

docs.title: 2. Install this exporter
docs.text:
apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter ucode-prometheus-exporter-full

When the package is installed, its uci-defaults script takes over what the old config sets into /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, once:

  • From the main section: listen_interface, listen_port, http_keepalive, cert, key and omit_zero_values.
  • From the ucode exporter, each named config collector section, option for option (wifi's stations).
  • When both old configs are there, the ucode exporter's.

It does so only while /etc/config/prometheus-exporter is as the package ships it. A port left at the old exporter's default (the ucode one's 9101) becomes 9100; a port you chose is kept. A value this exporter would refuse is left at its default. The old config file stays as it was.

docs.title: 3. Check what it took
docs.text:
logread -e prometheus-exporter | grep -e imported -e 'left at the default' -e 'nothing imported'
uci show prometheus-exporter

The log names every option it took, and every value it left at the default and why. See Log messages.

docs.title: 4. Update Prometheus
docs.text:
• The port. If the old exporter was the ucode one on 9101, scrape 9100, or set listen_port back to 9101.
  • The metric names. They are not the old exporters': most follow node_exporter, and every change is in Renamed metrics. Update the queries, alerts and recording rules that use an old name. Dashboards made for node_exporter work as they are.
  • The collectors. A query that selected collectors with collect[]= still does; collect=, the ucode exporter's spelling, too.
  • WireGuard peer names. The old exporters labelled peers with their description always; this one only with uci set prometheus-exporter.wireguard=collector; uci set prometheus-exporter.wireguard.peer_names=1; uci commit prometheus-exporter; service prometheus-exporter reload. See Security model for why it is off.

docs.title: If nothing was imported
docs.text: /etc/config/prometheus-exporter is not as the package ships it: nothing imported from /etc/config/<old> means the new config had been changed already. Set the options by hand: UCI configuration.

docs.title: How to Monitor SQM and CAKE
docs.text: The qdisc collector reads each network device's root queueing discipline with tc: what it sent, dropped and holds, with node_exporter's names. Where SQM shapes with CAKE, it also reads CAKE's capacity, memory and, per tin, its traffic, drops, ECN marks and delays.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • SQM is set up on the device, with cake as its queueing discipline (sqm-scripts, its layer_cake.qos or piece_of_cake.qos).

docs.title: 1. Install the qdisc collector
docs.text:
apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter-qdisc

It brings tc. It is in the -network and -full groups too.

docs.title: 2. Find the devices SQM shapes
docs.text:
SQM puts CAKE as the root qdisc of the interface it shapes, for upload, and of an ifb4<device> it makes for download:

prometheus-exporter qdisc | grep '^node_qdisc_cake_capacity_estimate_bytes_per_second'

node_qdisc_cake_capacity_estimate_bytes_per_second{device="eth1"} 2500000
node_qdisc_cake_capacity_estimate_bytes_per_second{device="ifb4eth1"} 11875000

Here eth1 is the WAN's upload, shaped to 20 Mbit/s, and ifb4eth1 its download, to 95 Mbit/s.

docs.title: 3. Query it
docs.text:
Drops per second, by device and tin:

rate(node_qdisc_cake_tin_drops_total[5m])

The worst queueing delay of each tin, which SQM is there to keep low:

node_qdisc_cake_tin_peak_delay_seconds

How much of the shaped rate the download uses, in bytes per second over bytes per second:

rate(node_qdisc_bytes_total{device="ifb4eth1"}[5m])
  / on (device) node_qdisc_cake_capacity_estimate_bytes_per_second

ECN marks, which CAKE uses before it drops:

rate(node_qdisc_cake_tin_ecn_marks_total[5m])

A tin is labeled by its index, as tc numbers them: a besteffort CAKE has tin 0 only, diffserv4 tins 0 to 3, Bulk to Voice.

docs.title: What it leaves out
docs.text:
Only the root qdisc of each device is read: SQM's ingress qdisc, which shapes nothing itself, a multiqueue NIC's per-queue children and HTB's leaves are left out, and so is noqueue, the qdisc of bridges, VLANs and WireGuard, whose counters are always 0. A device SQM does not shape still shows its default qdisc, fq_codel, with node_qdisc_* and no node_qdisc_cake_*.

Every family is in Metrics.

docs.title: How to Publish Metrics from Scripts
docs.text: The textfile collector serves the metrics of every *.prom file in a directory, /var/prometheus by default, as node_exporter's textfile collector does. A script on the device, run by cron or a hotplug event, writes what it knows there.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • ucode-prometheus-exporter-textfile, or the -full group, is installed.

docs.title: 1. Write the file
docs.text:
A file holds metrics in the Prometheus text format: # HELP and # TYPE lines, then samples. Write it to a temporary file in the same directory and rename it into place, so a scrape never reads half of it:

#!/bin/sh
# /usr/bin/apk-metrics: how many packages can be upgraded.
dir=/var/prometheus
tmp=$(mktemp "$dir/.apk.XXXXXX")
n=$(apk list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
cat >"$tmp" <<EOF
# HELP apk_upgradable_packages Packages with an upgrade available.
# TYPE apk_upgradable_packages gauge
apk_upgradable_packages $n
EOF
chmod 0644 "$tmp"
mv -f "$tmp" "$dir/apk.prom"

The temporary file's name must not end in .prom: the collector would read it.

docs.title: 2. Run it
docs.text:
From cron, every hour:

chmod +x /usr/bin/apk-metrics
echo '0 * * * * /usr/bin/apk-metrics' >>/etc/crontabs/root
service cron restart

docs.title: 3. Check it
docs.text:
prometheus-exporter textfile

The file's metrics are there, with node_textfile_mtime_seconds{file="/var/prometheus/apk.prom"}, when it was last written, and node_textfile_scrape_error 0.

docs.title: If a file is left out
docs.text:
A file that cannot be read, is not valid text format, gives a family another type than an earlier file did, repeats a series an earlier file has, or writes one of textfile's own families, is left out whole. node_textfile_scrape_error is then 1, and the log says which file and why:

logread -e prometheus-exporter | grep textfile

daemon.warn prometheus-exporter[1]: collector 'textfile': skipped /var/prometheus/apk.prom: EXPOSITION_INVALID (line 3: ...)

The collector itself still succeeds. Alert on node_textfile_scrape_error == 1, and on a node_textfile_mtime_seconds too old for how often the script runs.

docs.title: Use another directory
docs.text:
uci set prometheus-exporter.textfile=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.textfile.directory=/var/lib/metrics
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

The directory must be an absolute path, and not one every service shares, such as /tmp or /var/run: the jail would refuse to mount it. The service makes it when it starts, if it is not there. Keep it on tmpfs (/var, /tmp) unless the metrics must survive a reboot: a script writing to flash wears it.

docs.title: How to Troubleshoot
docs.text: Start from what is wrong: the service, one collector, or the scrape as Prometheus sees it.

docs.title: The service does not run
docs.text:
service prometheus-exporter status
logread -e prometheus-exporter
status or the log says Do disabled (option enabled in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter) uci set prometheus-exporter.main.enabled=1, commit, service prometheus-exporter start. invalid configuration, not starting, after the lines that say why Fix the option it names: service prometheus-exporter check shows the same as FAIL lines. See UCI configuration. deferring start until listen interface <name> becomes ready The interface has no address yet. It starts once it has one; check ifstatus <name>, or listen elsewhere: How to listen on the LAN. basic auth takes HTTPS only, and <cert> or <key> is missing: not starting The TLS files are not there. See How to serve HTTPS with basic auth. cannot make <path>: <error> The service could not make a directory: tmpfs is full, or the path is wrong.

A reload with an invalid configuration keeps the running exporter, and logs invalid configuration, keeping the running instance.

docs.title: A collector fails
docs.text:
check runs a scrape and says, for each collector, whether it succeeded, failed and why, or had nothing to observe and why:

service prometheus-exporter check

warn scrape: dnsmasq: UBUS_CALL_FAILED (dnsmasq metrics: Not found)
ok   scrape: wifi has nothing to observe: no wireless radios
  • Nothing to observe is not a failure: the device has no such hardware, kernel feature, or running service. The collector succeeds without samples, and its node_scrape_collector_observing is 0. If you do not want it, disable it. Each collector's cases are in Collectors.

  • A failure is a warn line with a code. Error codes says what each means. Under procd, each failing scrape also logs it at warning:

    logread -e prometheus-exporter | grep "collector '"

The same is on LuCI's Status → Prometheus exporter page, and in the ubus object's status:

ubus call prometheus-exporter status

docs.title: A collector works in check and fails under procd
docs.text:
check, the ubus object's status, LuCI's status page and the prometheus-exporter command run outside the jail, as root. Prometheus's scrapes run in it. A collector that only fails there lacks something the jail does not give it.

  1. See what the jail gives it:

    service prometheus-exporter check | grep '^warn jail'
ubus call service list '{"name":"prometheus-exporter"}'

    check warns of a path or program it cannot mount; procd's list shows what it mounted.

  2. A path that was not there when the service started is mounted once it is: check says <path> is not there; the service mounts it once it is, and the watch instance reloads the service when it appears. To mount it at once, service prometheus-exporter restart.

  3. A program that is not installed is a jail: <collector>: command <name> is not on ... warning: install its package.

What the jail holds is in The jail.

docs.title: Prometheus cannot scrape it
docs.text: Prometheus says Do connection refused The exporter does not listen where Prometheus asks. service prometheus-exporter status says where it listens; by default, loopback only. See How to listen on the LAN. A timeout The firewall drops it, or a collector's programs take too long: see How to give programs more time. 400 Bad Request The scrape's collect[] names a collector that is not installed, or is disabled. The body says which. 401 Unauthorized The user or password is wrong. server returned HTTP status 403 Forbidden Basic auth is on and the request came over HTTP: use scheme: https. 500 Internal Server Error Basic auth's file is broken: service prometheus-exporter restart writes it afresh.

docs.title: The metrics are not what you expect
docs.text:
• A name changed from the feed's exporters: see Renamed metrics.
  • A label is missing: a collector leaves out a label it has no value for.
  • Counters that are 0 are missing: option omit_zero_values '1' leaves them out.
  • What the scrape says of itself: node_scrape_collector_success 0 for a failure, node_scrape_collector_observing 0 for nothing to observe, node_scrape_collector_duration_seconds for the time each took.
node_scrape_collector_success == 0

alerts on a failing collector, and leaves alone one with nothing to observe.

docs.title: How to Monitor Unbound
docs.text: The unbound collector reads Unbound's statistics from its control socket, a Unix socket. OpenWrt's unbound package makes none: you turn it on, at the path the collector looks for.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Unbound runs on the device (unbound-daemon), enabled.
  • ucode-prometheus-exporter-unbound is installed. It brings ucode-mod-socket.

docs.title: 1. Give Unbound a control socket
docs.text:
Add to /etc/unbound/unbound_ext.conf:

remote-control:
    control-enable: yes
    control-interface: /var/lib/unbound/unbound.ctl

and restart Unbound:

service unbound restart

/var/lib/unbound is the directory the package makes for Unbound alone; Unbound makes the socket there when it starts.

docs.title: 2. Check it
docs.text:
ls -l /var/lib/unbound/unbound.ctl
prometheus-exporter unbound | grep unbound_queries_total

The service mounts the socket's directory in its jail. At boot Unbound starts after the exporter: the directory is mounted a few seconds after Unbound makes it, and the first scrapes until then fail. check warns of it meanwhile:

warn jail: unbound: /var/lib/unbound is not there; the service mounts it once it is

docs.title: Use another socket
docs.text:
If Unbound's socket is elsewhere, tell the collector:

uci set prometheus-exporter.unbound=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.unbound.socket=/var/lib/unbound/control.sock
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

The jail mounts the socket's directory, never the socket. That directory must be Unbound's own: one every service shares, such as /run or /var/run, is refused, and the collector cannot reach the socket there.

The jail then also holds what else is in that directory: in /var/lib/unbound, Unbound's generated config and root.key, and the TLS keys of unbound-control if its setup made them, all read-only.

docs.title: If it fails
docs.text: check or the log says Cause unbound has nothing to observe: unbound is disabled Unbound's init script is disabled. Nothing is wrong. SOCKET_FAILED (/var/lib/unbound/unbound.ctl: ... No such file or directory) No socket: step 1 is missing, or Unbound has not restarted. SOCKET_FAILED (...: no reply for 1000 ms) Unbound did not answer in a second.

docs.title: Remove a collector
docs.text:
apk del ucode-prometheus-exporter-wifi

The service reloads without it. A collector of the base package cannot be removed this way: disable it instead. A collector a group installed stays while the group is installed: remove the group, or keep the group and disable the collector.

docs.title: Remove the exporter
docs.text:
Remove the base package and everything that depends on it, the collector packages, the groups and the LuCI app with it:

apk del -r ucode-prometheus-exporter

The service stops, and rpcd no longer serves the prometheus-exporter ubus object. If you changed /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, apk keeps it; remove it if you do not want it:

rm -f /etc/config/prometheus-exporter

What the service made at run time, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/ and textfile's /var/prometheus/, is on tmpfs and goes at the next reboot.

If Prometheus scrapes the device, take it out of the scrape configuration, or its target stays down.

docs.title: How to Upgrade the Exporter
docs.text: Every collector package, group and the LuCI app depends on the base package of the very same version, so they move together.

docs.title: Before you upgrade
docs.text: Read what the new version changes. Before 1.0.0 a minor version may rename metrics or options: see About versions. A renamed metric breaks the queries and dashboards that use the old name.

docs.title: From a feed
docs.text:
apk update
apk upgrade

docs.title: From .apk files
docs.text:
Copy every package you have installed, in the new version, to the device's /tmp, and add them in one command:

apk add --allow-untrusted /tmp/ucode-prometheus-exporter-*0.2.0-r1.apk /tmp/luci-app-prometheus-exporter-0.2.0-r1.apk

Adding the base package alone fails: the installed collectors still want the old version.

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | grep build_info
service prometheus-exporter check

ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version="..."} is the new version. The upgrade restarts a running service; /etc/config/prometheus-exporter stays as you had it. If you changed it, apk may leave the new version's file beside it, as /etc/config/prometheus-exporter.apk-new: compare the two, and remove it once you have taken what you want.

docs.title: How to Run the Benchmark
docs.text: The benchmark times each collector and whole scrapes on generated worlds: what a router's /proc, /sys, ubus, netlink and programs would give. Run it to see what a change costs, here, in a container limited as a slower router, on a device, or in QEMU as a MIPS router.

docs.title: In the development environment
docs.text:
make bench

It prints a table and writes bin/bench/devenv.json, and checks the budgets of test/bench/budgets.uc: scaling and memory always, times too when the container is unconstrained. CI runs the same.

Narrow it to some cases, or run each more:

make bench FILTER='typical/scrape'
make bench FILTER='nat_traffic' BENCH_ARGS='-r 20'

-r N runs each case at least N times, -t S for at least S seconds.

docs.title: Before and after a change
docs.text:
Bench another revision's src/ with this checkout's benchmark:

make bench BENCH_REV=main
make bench

The results are bin/bench/devenv-main.json and bin/bench/devenv.json.

docs.title: As a slower router
docs.text:
Limit the container to a share of one CPU:

make bench FILTER='calibrate' BENCH_CPUS=0.35 BENCH_CPUSET=0

Pick BENCH_CPUS by calibrate:vm's loop turn, in the same session: the share that makes it match the router's. A container's programs still cost what the host's do, so its whole scrapes are faster than the router's; QEMU is the closer model of a MIPS router. The calibration is in Performance on small routers.

BENCH_MEMORY=64m limits its memory too.

docs.title: On a device
docs.text:
make bench-device HOST=root@router.lan

The sources, the benchmark and the worlds are copied to the device's /tmp, run there with its own ucode, beside whatever it runs, and removed afterwards; nothing is installed. The device needs ucode, ucode-mod-fs, -ubus, -uci, -rtnl and -log. The result is bin/bench/<HOST>.json, or BENCH_DEVICE_LABEL= names it.

docs.title: In QEMU, as a MIPS router
docs.text:
make bench-qemu
make bench-qemu QEMU_SHIFT=2

OpenWrt's malta target in qemu-system-mipsel: a MIPS 24Kc, mipsel_24kc packages as MT7621-class routers have, with the built packages installed from the release's feed. QEMU_SHIFT=1 runs it at 500 MIPS, 2 at 250. It downloads the release's images and packages the first time, into bin/qemu/, and it is slow: narrow it with FILTER=.

The worlds are generated by test/bench/gen.uc from a seed, with the fixtures as templates, so every machine reads the same; make bench-worlds writes them to bin/bench/worlds/. What the cases are, and what the results mean, is in Performance on small routers.

docs.title: How to Write Documentation
docs.text: The documentation is built with MkDocs Material, inside Docker. You need Docker and make.

docs.title: Preview while you write
docs.text:
make docs-serve

Open http://localhost:8000. The page reloads when you save a file under docs/ or change mkdocs.yml. If port 8000 is taken, choose another: make docs-serve DOCS_PORT=8001.

docs.title: Build the site
docs.text:
make docs

The site goes to bin/site/, and make -C docs clean removes it. The build runs mkdocs build --strict, so a broken link or any other warning fails it. CI runs the same strict build on pushes and pull requests to main that touch the docs, and a second one with the versioned config, mkdocs.mike.yml (make docs-mike locally).

Merging to main publishes nothing: the docs go online with the next release. To correct the docs already online, see How to fix the docs of the released version; what publishes when is in Documentation publishing.

docs.title: Where a page goes
docs.text:
Pick the folder by what the reader is doing, following Diátaxis:

Folder The reader is... Example tutorials/ learning by doing, guided step by step Monitor a router with Prometheus how-to/ working toward a goal they already have Serve HTTPS with basic auth reference/ looking up a fact Every option of the configuration explanation/ trying to understand why Nothing to observe

Keep one type per page and link to the others instead of mixing them. Add every new page to nav in mkdocs.yml and to the index.md of its folder. Link between pages with relative paths, never with the site's URL, so each published version links to itself.

The reasoning a reader needs lives in the explanation pages: when a change rests on a new reason, write it there, in the same change. Code and test comments follow the same rule: give the reason in a few words, or point to the explanation page that holds it.

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text:
Four reference pages are written from the code by make docs-gen, and never by hand:

Page From docs/reference/collectors.md Each collector's meta, the package Makefile, and the code's reasons for nothing to observe. docs/reference/metrics.md What each collector writes when it runs on the fixture sets of test/fixtures/. docs/reference/uci-config.md config.uc's option specs and datatypes. docs/reference/error-codes.md errors.uc, and where each code is raised.

What the code does not say is in docs/gen/notes.uc: when each collector has nothing to observe, what a computed jail path is, the patterns that fold a driver's statistics into one row, the families no fixture shows, the meaning of each error code, and a name for each fixture set. The generator checks the notes against the code and refuses, writing nothing, an entry the code contradicts.

  1. Change the code, or the notes.

  2. Regenerate:

    make docs-gen

  3. If it refuses, its message says which note to change: a new collector that can have nothing to observe needs an entry in nothing_to_observe; a family the collector declares that no fixture makes it write needs a fixture, or an entry in unharvested; a new fixture set needs a name in capture_sets, which keeps the device's own name out of the docs.

  4. Commit the pages with the change. make lint fails while a page is not what make docs-gen would write.

docs.title: Keep it true
docs.text:
Reference pages describe the code as it is. When you change one of these, update its page in the same change:

Code Reference page A collector, config.uc, errors.uc, the package Makefile, test/fixtures/ The generated pages: make docs-gen. files/etc/init.d/prometheus-exporter, check.uc, status.uc Service commands cli.uc, files/usr/bin/prometheus-exporter The prometheus-exporter command http.uc, app.uc, auth.uc, query.uc, scrape.uc HTTP endpoint rpc.uc, the rpcd plugin ubus object luci/ LuCI app, How to use the LuCI app jail.uc, state.uc, the init script's mounts The jail loader.uc, deps.uc, result.uc, services.uc, exposition.uc's recorder Collector interface A log line Log messages files/, the package Makefile Files and packages The root Makefile, docs/Makefile Make targets docs/Makefile, devenv/scripts/docs-*.sh, .github/workflows/docs.yml, mkdocs.mike.yml, docs/overrides/, devenv/gh-pages/, devenv/services/docs/ Documentation publishing migrate.uc How to move from the feed's exporters A renamed metric Renamed metrics

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Use generic names (router, ap) and documentation addresses: 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24 for IPv4, 2001:db8::/32 for IPv6. Never paste a real device's name, MAC address, SSID, key or public address.
  • Output captured from the lab is the exception: paste it as it is. Its addresses are docker's and disposable.
  • Use Mermaid in a fenced block with the mermaid language, only where a picture explains more than a paragraph.

docs.title: How to Fix the Docs of the Released Version
docs.text: A docs fix reaches the published site through the docs branch of the newest minor, docs/X.Y: pushing the branch republishes /X.Y/. Only the newest minor gets fixes; older versions stay as they are. The examples fix 0.2.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The fix is merged into main. Fixes always land on main first.
  • The fix changes only files under docs/, mkdocs.yml or mkdocs.mike.yml. A code fix needs a release instead: How to publish the docs of a patch release.

docs.title: 1. Cherry-pick the fix onto the docs branch
docs.text:
git fetch origin --tags
git switch docs/0.2
git cherry-pick <sha>

Cherry-pick each commit you need. Never merge or rebase main into docs/0.2: it would publish the docs of unreleased work (why).

If a commit also changes files outside the docs, take only its docs part:

git cherry-pick -n <sha>
git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- . ':!docs/' ':!mkdocs.yml' ':!mkdocs.mike.yml'
git commit -C <sha>

docs.title: 2. Check the branch
docs.text:
devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh docs/0.2

It prints the release tag when the branch may publish. If it refuses, see below.

docs.title: 3. Push
docs.text:
git push origin docs/0.2

The docs workflow republishes /0.2/. Check that its publish job succeeded.

docs.title: If the guard refuses
docs.text:
The message tells you which case you are in; every message is listed in Docs-only guard.

  • docs/0.2 changes files outside docs/: <files>; code fixes need a release: a commit on the branch changes code. If you have not pushed yet, drop it with git reset --hard origin/docs/0.2 and cherry-pick again as in step 1. If it is already pushed, revert it and push the revert:

    git revert <sha>
git push origin docs/0.2

    The code fix ships with the next release.

  • v0.2.1 is not an ancestor of docs/0.2: a patch release was tagged and the branch has not moved to it. Move it as in How to publish the docs of a patch release, then push again.

  • docs/0.2 has no v0.2.* release tag: the tags are missing locally. Run git fetch origin --tags. In CI, the minor has not been released yet, and the branch should not exist.

docs.title: How to Capture Fixtures from a Device
docs.text: The tests, the benchmark's worlds and the metrics reference read what real devices answered, from test/fixtures/<set>/. Capture a device's answers when you write a collector for something the sets do not have yet.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• ssh access to the device, as root, with ucode on it (OpenWrt 25.12 has it).
  • The device runs what the collector reads.

docs.title: 1. Say what to read
docs.text:
Add the sources to test/fixtures/SOURCES, one per line:

Line Captures file PATH The file, or every file the glob matches, at its own path. ubus OBJECT METHOD [ARGS] The reply, as ubus/OBJECT.METHOD.json. link GLOB Where each symlink the glob matches leads, into links.json. uci CONFIG The config's sections, as uci/CONFIG.json, without secret options (keys, passwords).

docs.title: 2. Capture
docs.text:
make fixtures HOST=root@router.lan NAME=my-router

Everything is read-only on the device. Only files not there yet are added to test/fixtures/my-router/, so the values tests assert on do not change under them; FORCE=1 replaces them all.

What make fixtures cannot read, capture by hand into the same set and say how in SOURCES' comments: a program's output as commands/<program>_<arguments>.txt (commands/ethtool_S_lan.txt for ethtool -S lan), an rtnetlink or nl80211 reply as rtnl/<CMD>.json or nl80211/<CMD>.<device>.json.

docs.title: 3. Redact
docs.text:
Before you commit, replace in every file of the set:

  • MAC addresses, with locally administered ones, 02:00:00:…;
  • public IP addresses, with 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24 or 2001:db8::/32;
  • SSIDs, hostnames, domain names, user names and keys.

uci captures leave out secret options, but not names and addresses.

docs.title: 4. Name the set in the docs
docs.text:
The metrics reference runs every collector on every set, and names each set without its device's name. Add the new set to capture_sets in docs/gen/notes.uc, then:

make docs-gen

What neither device has is written by hand in test/fixtures/synthetic/, each file with the format it follows in test/fixtures/synthetic/SOURCES.

docs.title: How to Use the Lab
docs.text: The lab is OpenWrt under procd in a privileged container, left running, with the built packages, every collector and the LuCI app installed: a device to try things on.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
make lab

It builds the packages, boots OpenWrt and installs them. When it is up:

The lab runs, as container ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab:
  LuCI      http://127.0.0.1:8080/  (root, no password)
  /metrics  http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics
  a shell   docker exec -it ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab ash
  stop it   make lab-down

If a port is taken, or another checkout runs a lab, give yours its own name and ports:

make lab LAB_NAME=my-lab LAB_LUCI_PORT=18080 LAB_METRICS_PORT=19100

docs.title: Try a change
docs.text: Edit the code, then run make lab again: it rebuilds the packages and starts the lab afresh, so nothing you changed by hand in it survives.

docs.title: Look inside
docs.text:
docker exec -it ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab ash

service prometheus-exporter check
logread -e prometheus-exporter
ubus call prometheus-exporter status

docs.title: Stop it
docs.text:
make lab-down

With LAB_NAME too, if you gave one.

docs.title: What is different from a device
docs.text:
• lan is the container's eth0, with the address docker gave it, and no bridge.
  • The firewall, mwan3 and chronyd do not start: fw4 would reject what docker forwards, mwan3 would rewrite the routing, and chronyd would steer the clock, which a privileged container shares with its host. Do not start chronyd there.
  • The exporter listens on every address (listen_interface '*'), which docker's published port needs.
  • Unbound listens on port 5353, with its control socket where the unbound collector looks.
  • textfile has a file to read, /var/prometheus/lab.prom.
  • ubnt-manager's sample radio is removed, or ssh to it would cost each scrape its 5 seconds.

The boot is devenv/services/lab/boot.sh, the setup devenv/services/lab/setup.sh.

docs.title: How to Package a Collector
docs.text: Every collector is in the base package or in a package of its own, ucode-prometheus-exporter-<name>. Both are declared in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • The collector, src/prometheus_exporter/collectors/<module>.uc, and its unit test. See Collector interface.

docs.title: 1. Choose its package
docs.text:
• The base package only for what every device has, and only when it needs nothing the base package does not bring. Add its module to BASE_COLLECTORS:

    BASE_COLLECTORS:=conntrack cpu ... uname vmstat <module>

  • A package of its own for anything else. Add a Collector line, in the order of the module names:

    $(eval $(call Collector,<module>,<name>,<what it collects>,<dependencies>))
    Argument Content <module> The module's file name, without .uc: ltq_dsl. <name> meta.name, the package's suffix: ltq-dsl. <what it collects> A few words, added to the package's title: Lantiq DSL line. No commas. <dependencies> +package for each package its needs and commands call for, space-separated: +ucode-mod-nl80211 for nl80211, +ucode-mod-socket for socket, the package of each program it runs. Empty for none.

    The macro makes a package that installs the module, depends on the base package of the same version, and reloads an enabled service when it is installed or removed.

docs.title: 2. Add it to a group
docs.text:
If every router or access point should have it, add its name to a group's list:

NETWORK_GROUP:=ethtool nat_traffic netstat nft-counters qdisc snmp6 sockstat <name>

FULL_GROUP holds the other three and more. Leave out a collector of particular hardware or of an optional service.

docs.title: 3. Check
docs.text:
make test
make docs-gen
make lint
make package-check
  • test/integration/collectors_test.uc holds every collector to one package, named after it, whose dependencies cover its needs and commands. A new program needs an entry in its COMMAND_PACKAGES.
  • make docs-gen adds it to the reference: its package and groups to Collectors, its families to Metrics. If it can have nothing to observe, or declares a family no fixture makes it write, the generator says what to add to docs/gen/notes.uc.
  • make package-check builds and installs every package, the new one too.
  • Add the collector to NOTICE when it ports an upstream collector.

docs.title: How to Publish the Docs of a New Minor Release
docs.text: A new minor release, such as 0.2.0, publishes its docs as /0.2/ and moves /latest/ to them. It also starts a new docs branch and freezes the previous one. The examples release 0.2.0 after 0.1.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Publishing is set up: How to set up documentation publishing.
  • The release is ready on main, with PKG_VERSION:=0.2.0 in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile.
  • Every pinned docs link in the shipped files points to /0.2/, including URL:= in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile. If the project keeps a CHANGELOG.md, the release's entries are under ## [0.2.0]. make lint passes.

docs.title: 1. Tag the release
docs.text:
git tag v0.2.0
git push origin v0.2.0

The docs workflow publishes /0.2/, titled 0.2.0, and moves latest to it. Check that its publish job succeeded and that /latest/ shows 0.2.0 in the version selector.

docs.title: 2. Create the docs branch
docs.text:
git branch docs/0.2 v0.2.0
git push origin docs/0.2

docs.title: 3. Freeze the previous branch
docs.text:
Stop pushing to docs/0.1. /0.1/ stays online as it was last published. From now on, doc fixes go to docs/0.2: see How to fix the docs of the released version.

What each push publishes, and when latest moves, is in Documentation publishing. Why only the newest minor gets fixes: About versioned documentation.

docs.title: How to Publish the Docs of a Patch Release
docs.text: A patch release, such as 0.2.1, republishes its minor, /0.2/, from the new tag. Afterwards the docs branch has to move onto the tag, or it cannot publish again. The examples release 0.2.1.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The minor's docs branch exists: How to publish the docs of a new minor release.
  • The release is ready, with PKG_VERSION:=0.2.1 in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, and make lint passes.

docs.title: 1. Tag the release
docs.text:
git tag v0.2.1
git push origin v0.2.1

The docs workflow republishes /0.2/, now titled 0.2.1. latest follows if 0.2 is the newest minor.

docs.title: 2. Move the docs branch to the tag
docs.text:
git fetch origin
git switch docs/0.2
git merge --ff-only v0.2.1

If the fast-forward fails because the branch has fix commits of its own, merge the tag instead:

git merge v0.2.1

If the merge conflicts, keep the tag's side for every file outside docs/, mkdocs.yml and mkdocs.mike.yml: the branch may only differ from the tag in the docs.

Then push:

git push origin docs/0.2

Until the branch contains v0.2.1, every publish from it is refused with v0.2.1 is not an ancestor of docs/0.2. See Docs-only guard.

docs.title: How to Republish a Version
docs.text: Republish a version when its publish failed or was cancelled, or when gh-pages lost it. The docs workflow can be run by hand for any release tag or docs branch. The examples republish 0.2.

docs.title: 1. Choose the ref
docs.text:
• If the minor has a docs branch, use it: docs/0.2. It holds the release plus its doc fixes.
  • Otherwise use the minor's newest release tag, for example v0.2.1.

Republishing an older tag than the newest, or a tag instead of the branch, replaces /0.2/ with older docs.

docs.title: 2. Run the workflow
docs.text:
In the repository, open Actions → docs → Run workflow, enter the ref, and run it. With the GitHub CLI:

gh workflow run docs.yml -f ref=docs/0.2

Republishing an older minor leaves latest on the newest one. A docs branch still has to pass the docs-only guard; if it refuses, see How to fix the docs of the released version.

docs.title: How to Set Up Documentation Publishing
docs.text: Nothing is published until the repository is on GitHub, the site's URL is known, and the first release is tagged. Do these steps once, in this order. The examples use the repository m00qek/ucode-prometheus-exporter, the site https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/, and 0.1.0 as the first release.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A GitHub repository for the exporter, with admin rights to change its Pages settings.
  • The first release, 0.1.0, is ready on main: PKG_VERSION:=0.1.0 in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile.

docs.title: 1. Push main
docs.text:
git remote add origin git@github.com:m00qek/ucode-prometheus-exporter.git
git push -u origin main

docs.title: 2. Set the site's URL and pin the links
docs.text:
1. In mkdocs.yml, check that site_url is the site's base URL, without a version, and repo_url the repository's. Change both if the repository has another owner or name:

    site_url: https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/
repo_url: https://github.com/m00qek/ucode-prometheus-exporter

  2. To give the packages a link to their docs, add URL:= to Package/$(PKG_NAME)/Default in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, pointing to the docs of the package's minor:

    URL:=https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/0.1/

  3. Link the README to https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/latest/.

  4. Check the pinned links:

    make lint

Commit the change and push it to main. Which link goes where is in Links to the documentation.

docs.title: 3. Tag the first release
docs.text:
git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0

The docs workflow creates gh-pages and publishes /0.1/ and /latest/. Wait for its publish job to succeed.

docs.title: 4. Turn on GitHub Pages
docs.text: In the repository's Settings → Pages, set the source to Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root). The site then answers at https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/, which redirects to /latest/.

docs.title: 5. Create the docs branch
docs.text:
git branch docs/0.1 v0.1.0
git push origin docs/0.1

Doc fixes for 0.1 go through this branch: see How to fix the docs of the released version.

docs.title: Clear an unversioned deploy from gh-pages
docs.text:
If gh-pages carries files from an earlier unversioned deploy, for example from mkdocs gh-deploy, remove them once: they shadow the 404 redirect and keep serving stale pages. Do it while no docs workflow is running.

  1. Check out gh-pages and list its root:

    git fetch origin gh-pages
git switch gh-pages
git ls-tree --name-only HEAD

  2. Remove everything that is not part of the versioned layout: the version folders, latest, versions.json, index.html, 404.html and .nojekyll stay.

    git ls-tree --name-only HEAD |
    grep -vxE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+|latest|versions\.json|index\.html|404\.html|\.nojekyll' |
    xargs git rm -r -q
git commit -m 'Remove the unversioned site'
git push origin gh-pages
git switch main

If gh-pages has not been published with mike yet, publish first (step 3), so that index.html is mike's redirect and not the old site's home page.

docs.title: How to Run the Tests
docs.text: Everything runs in Docker, on OpenWrt's own images, on the release in OPENWRT_VERSION (25.12.5 by default). You need Docker and make.

docs.title: Unit and integration tests
docs.text:
make test

make unit and make integration run one suite. To narrow a run:

make unit MODULES=test/unit/prometheus_exporter/collectors/wifi_test.uc
make test FILTER='collectors.wifi' VERBOSE=1
make watch

watch runs the tests again whenever a file under src/, test/, files/, devenv/scripts/ or docs/gen/ changes. To run them on the API floor, the first 25.12 release, as CI does too: make test OPENWRT_VERSION=25.12.0.

docs.title: Lint
docs.text:
make lint

It loads every module on the release's ucode, so a function that ucode lacks fails here and not on a router. It also fails when the translation template or a generated reference page is out of date: run make pot or make docs-gen, and commit the result.

docs.title: The packages
docs.text:
make package-check

Builds the apks with the SDK, installs them offline in an OpenWrt image, scrapes a real uhttpd and calls the ubus object in a real rpcd, with the base package alone and then with the LuCI app.

docs.title: The service under procd
docs.text:
make e2e

Boots OpenWrt in a privileged container, without network, and checks the service in its jail as packages come and go and its configuration changes. It needs Docker to allow privileged containers.

docs.title: The LuCI app
docs.text:
make browser
make browser FILTER='settings'

Runs the Playwright tests of test/browser/ against LuCI with the built packages. Screenshots, and on a failure the error context and LuCI's log, are in bin/browser/.

docs.title: The documentation tooling
docs.text:
make docs-test
make docs

docs-test runs the publishing scripts' tests; docs builds the site, strictly. See How to write documentation.

CI runs lint, test and package-check on 25.12.0 and 25.12.5, e2e on both, bench, and browser; and the docs workflow builds the site. Every target is in Make targets.

docs.title: How to Update the Translation Template
docs.text: The LuCI app's strings, every _('...') of luci/, are in the translation template luci/po/templates/prometheus-exporter.pot. make lint fails while it is out of date.

docs.title: Update it
docs.text:
After you add, change or move a string in the LuCI app:

make pot

It runs openwrt/luci's own scanner, build/i18n-scan.pl, over luci/ laid out as applications/luci-app-prometheus-exporter of the luci tree, so the template's location comments are the ones upstream would write. Commit the template with the change.

docs.title: If it fails
docs.text:
pot: the scanner warned, so a string may be missing from the template means the scanner lost its way in a file: it printed which, above. Fix the string it stumbled on, often a quote inside _(), and run it again. It writes nothing while it warns.

The scanner runs in its own image, ucode-prometheus-exporter-i18n, from devenv/services/i18n/Dockerfile, without network.

docs.title: Collector Interface
docs.text:
A collector is a ucode module, src/prometheus_exporter/collectors/<module>.uc, installed to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter/collectors/. It exports meta and collect:

'use strict';

import * as Result from 'prometheus_exporter.result';
import * as errors from 'prometheus_exporter.errors';
import { first_line, fields } from 'prometheus_exporter.proc';

export const meta = {
    name: 'loadavg',
    title: 'Load average',
    help: 'Load averages from /proc/loadavg.',
    needs: [ 'fs' ],
};

export function collect(deps, out) {
    let line = first_line(deps.fs, '/proc/loadavg');

    if (line == null)
        return Result.err(errors.SOURCE_UNREADABLE, '/proc/loadavg');

    let x = fields(line);
    if (length(x) < 3)
        return Result.err(errors.SOURCE_INVALID, `/proc/loadavg: ${sprintf('%J', line)}`);

    out.gauge('node_load1', '1m load average.')(null, x[0]);
    out.gauge('node_load5', '5m load average.')(null, x[1]);
    out.gauge('node_load15', '15m load average.')(null, x[2]);

    return Result.ok();
};

That is loadavg, as the base package installs it.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
The loader (src/prometheus_exporter/loader.uc) takes every file of the collectors' directory named [a-z0-9_]+.uc, imports it, and validates its exports. A module that does not import, or whose meta or collect is not valid, is left out, and the rest load: the handler logs it at err, check and the ubus object's collectors list it. The collectors are sorted by name.

uhttpd loads them once, when it starts; a scrape runs what was loaded. Installing or removing a collector package reloads the service, which restarts uhttpd.

docs.title: meta
docs.text: Field Required Type Rules name yes string [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*, and the module's name with _ for -: ltq-dsl in ltq_dsl.uc. What collect[] takes, and the suffix of its package. title yes string 1 to 40 characters, no control characters: a label for lists and forms. help yes string A sentence: what it collects, and from where. needs yes array Capabilities from needs, once each. All it gets in deps. configs with uci array The uci configs it reads, [a-z0-9_-]+, not prometheus-exporter: its own settings come as options. Not allowed without uci. commands with exec array The programs it runs. Not allowed without exec. optional_commands no array Those of commands it runs only where they are installed: no package it depends on has them, and the jail does without them. timeout no integer With exec: the seconds its programs get in all per scrape, 1 to 30, unless its section sets timeout. Without it, the main section's exec_timeout. options no object Its own options, { <name>: { default, help, datatype } }. See Options. paths no array What it reads outside procfs and sysfs, with fs, socket or exec in needs. See The jail.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Key Required Rules (the name) [a-z][a-z0-9_]*; not enabled nor timeout, which are the core's. default yes A boolean, an integer or a string: it sets the option's type. help yes A sentence: what the option does. datatype no One of the datatypes the core checks: uinteger, range(min,max), directory, file, regex. It must take the default. See UCI configuration.

collect gets the options typed, the defaults for those unset. A value that does not fit fails the collector with CONFIG_INVALID in each scrape.

docs.title: collect(deps, out, options)
docs.text:
Argument Content deps One capability per entry of meta.needs, by name. out The recorder the collector writes its families to. options Its own options, typed.

It returns a Result. Anything else fails it with COLLECTOR_NO_RESULT; an exception, with COLLECTOR_CRASHED. What it recorded is kept when it fails, and dropped when it has nothing to observe.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
prometheus_exporter.result:

Call Means node_scrape_collector_success node_scrape_collector_observing Logged Result.ok() It observed what it reads. 1 1 No Result.err(code, details, data) It failed: code from prometheus_exporter.errors, details a string for the log. 0 1 At warning: collector '<name>': CODE (details) Result.none(reason) Nothing to observe: its hardware, kernel feature or service is not there. Its samples are dropped. 1 0 No

Result.is(r) tells a Result, Result.is_none(r) one of nothing to observe, Result.describe(r) gives CODE (details).

docs.title: prometheus_exporter.services
docs.text:
For a collector to tell nothing to observe from a failure, over deps.ubus:

Function Returns unless_disabled(ubus, name, failure) Result.none('<name> is disabled') or Result.none('<name> is not installed') when rpcd's rc says the init script name is not enabled or not there; failure otherwise, or when rc cannot say. idle(ubus, name) That reason, or null. state(ubus, name) A Result of enabled, disabled or not installed. object_missing(res) Whether a ubus call failed for its object not being there (Not found).

docs.title: needs
docs.text:
Only prometheus_exporter.deps touches the system. A collector gets the capabilities it names, and a scrape's collectors share one ubus connection and one uci cursor.

Need deps.<need> fs readfile, open, lsdir, glob, stat, realpath of the fs module. Nothing that writes. ubus call(object, method, args) and list(), as Results. A failed call is UBUS_CALL_FAILED with data.status, libubus's text, as Not found. uci deps.uci.<config> for each of meta.configs, read-only, the committed configuration only: loaded(), get(section, option), get_all(section), sections(type), foreach(type, cb). rtnl request(cmd, flags, attrs) as a Result (RTNL_FAILED), and const. nl80211 The same, for nl80211 (NL80211_FAILED). Needs ucode-mod-nl80211. socket unix_request(path, message, timeout_ms): the whole reply of a Unix stream socket's server, as a Result (SOCKET_FAILED). Needs ucode-mod-socket. exec run(argv): a program of meta.commands, without a shell's interpretation of its arguments, its standard output as a Result. See Programs. time now(): the system time, in seconds. log log(msg): a line at warning, collector '<name>': <msg>, for what a collector that succeeds still has to say.

A need the system lacks (nl80211, socket) fails the collector with NEED_MISSING.

docs.title: Programs
docs.text:
• A program not in meta.commands is COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED, without running.
  • Its standard error is discarded. An exit status other than 0 is COMMAND_FAILED, with data.status; one that cannot start, COMMAND_FAILED with data.status null.
  • A collector's programs get, in all per scrape, the seconds of its section's timeout, else meta.timeout, else the main section's exec_timeout (5), at most 30. The shell counts whole seconds: they take at most one second more.
  • One still running then is killed, with every process it started, and is COMMAND_TIMEOUT with data.timed_out. So is any run after the seconds are spent, without running.

docs.title: out
docs.text:
prometheus_exporter.exposition's recorder:

Call Does out.gauge(name, help), out.counter(name, help), out.untyped(name, help) Declares a family, and returns (labels, value), which records a sample and returns itself, so calls chain. out.labels(labels) Makes a label set several samples share, once, to pass in place of the object. out.parse(text) Adds exposition text, which must be valid as a whole: a Result, EXPOSITION_INVALID otherwise.
  • labels is an object, or null for none. A label whose value is null is left out.
  • A value that is not a number is skipped: null, an empty string, a word. A string of digits, or of hex as in sysfs flags, is read as one. true and false are 1 and 0.
  • Names are made valid: every character the format does not allow is an underscore.
  • A family declared twice with two types keeps the first, and logs a warning.

docs.title: The prometheus-exporter Command
docs.text:
/usr/bin/prometheus-exporter prints a scrape on standard output, as /metrics answers it. The base package installs it.

usage: prometheus-exporter [-h] [-l] [-d DIR] [COLLECTOR...]
  -h      show this help
  -l      list the installed collectors
  -d DIR  load the collectors from DIR

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description COLLECTOR... The collectors to scrape, by name (ltq-dsl) or module (ltq_dsl), in that order. Without any, every enabled collector, as a scrape without collect[]. Each is passed as collect[]=<name>: see HTTP endpoint. -l Print one line per installed collector, its name and its help, and exit. -d DIR Load the collectors from DIR instead of /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter/collectors. -h Print the usage and exit.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status When 0 The scrape was printed, or -l or -h was given. 1 The scrape was refused: a collector that is not installed, or one that is disabled. Its message is on standard error, as COLLECTOR_INVALID (unknown collector 'nope'). 2 An option it does not take. The usage is on standard error.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• It reads the committed configuration, as the service does: a collector disabled in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter is left out, and naming it is refused.
  • What the exporter logs goes to standard error, whatever its level: a collector that fails, a module the loader leaves out.
  • It runs as the user who runs it, outside the jail. A collector that works here and fails under the service lacks something in the jail: see The jail.
  • It never compresses and never asks for basic auth: those are the HTTP endpoint's.
  • The build info's version is the package's, <version>-r<release>, or dev from a source tree.

docs.text:
prometheus-exporter -l
prometheus-exporter loadavg
prometheus-exporter wifi ltq-dsl

$ prometheus-exporter loadavg
# HELP node_load1 1m load average.
# TYPE node_load1 gauge
node_load1 0.72
...
