docs.title: Documentation Publishing
docs.text: The documentation is published with mike to the gh-pages branch, one version per minor release, by the docs workflow in .github/workflows/docs.yml. The make targets that build and test it locally are in Make targets. For the reasons behind this design, see About versioned documentation.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
Event Ref Job Publishes Version title Push of a tag v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+, for example v0.2.1 publish version X.Y X.Y.Z, the tag without its v Push to a branch docs/[0-9]+.[0-9]+, for example docs/0.2 publish version X.Y, if the docs-only guard passes the newest vX.Y.* tag without its v Push to a branch main build nothing — Pull request into main build nothing — Manual run (workflow_dispatch) the input ref: a release tag vX.Y.Z or a branch docs/X.Y publish as for a push of that ref as for a push of that ref

Branch pushes and pull requests start the workflow only when they change at least one of these paths. Tag pushes and manual runs always start it.

  • docs/**
  • mkdocs.yml, mkdocs.mike.yml
  • devenv/gh-pages/**
  • devenv/scripts/docs-*.sh
  • devenv/services/docs/**
  • test/docs/**
  • .github/workflows/docs.yml

Nothing else publishes: main, pull requests and pre-release tags such as v0.3.0-rc1 never reach gh-pages.

docs.title: build
docs.text:
Runs on pull requests and on pushes to main.

  1. make -C docs build: strict build with mkdocs.yml.
  2. make -C docs build-mike: strict build with mkdocs.mike.yml.
  3. make -C docs test: the shell and Node tests in test/docs/. The generator's tests in test/docs/gen/ run with make test.

docs.title: publish
docs.text:
Runs on release tags, docs/* branches and manual runs. REF is the manual run's ref input, or else the pushed ref.

  1. Checks out REF with its full history and tags.
  2. Installs Python 3.12 and devenv/services/docs/requirements.txt with pip.
  3. Sets the git committer to github-actions[bot].
  4. mkdocs build --strict --config-file mkdocs.mike.yml.
  5. devenv/scripts/docs-publish.sh "$REF".

docs.title: Permissions and concurrency
docs.text:
Setting Value Workflow permissions contents: read publish permissions contents: write publish concurrency group gh-pages, with cancel-in-progress: false

One publish job runs at a time; a later one waits. GitHub keeps at most one waiting job per concurrency group: a newer one cancels the one already waiting.

docs.title: The latest rule
docs.text:
A publish of version X.Y also points latest to X.Y, and makes latest the default version, only if X.Y is the newest of the version folders already on gh-pages together with X.Y itself, compared with sort -V: 0.10 is newer than 0.9. Otherwise latest stays where it is. The first publish always takes latest.

The script prints which case applied:

publishing 0.10 (0.10.0) as latest
publishing 0.9 (0.9.1); latest stays on 0.10

docs.title: Site layout
docs.text:
The published site on gh-pages:

Path Written by Content /X.Y/ mike One folder per minor, without a v: 0.9, 0.10. /latest/ mike A full copy of the newest minor's folder (alias_type: copy), not a symlink or a redirect. /versions.json mike The versions, their titles and aliases, for the version selector. /index.html mike Redirects to /latest/ (mike set-default latest). /404.html docs-publish.sh Copy of devenv/gh-pages/404.html. See below. /.nojekyll docs-publish.sh Empty. Tells GitHub Pages to serve the files as they are.

Every page carries a version selector. With site_url set, its canonical URL is the same page under /latest/ (canonical_version: latest). Pages of a version that is not latest show a banner, docs/overrides/main.html:

You are reading the documentation of an older release. Go to the latest.

The link goes to the site's root, which redirects to /latest/.

docs.title: 404 redirect
docs.text:
GitHub Pages serves /404.html for every missing path. Its script redirects /<site>/<path> to /<site>/latest/<path>, keeping the query string and the #anchor. /<site> and /<site>/ go to /<site>/latest/.

It does not redirect, and shows "Page not found", when the first segment after /<site>/ is latest, dev or a version X.Y, or when the path is /. The first path segment is always taken as the site, so the redirect works only on a project site, https://<user>.github.io/<site>/.

docs.title: Docs-only guard
docs.text:
devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh runs before every publish of a docs/X.Y branch, whether pushed or run manually. It does not run for release tags. It checks the checked-out commit, HEAD, against the release tag of its minor:

  1. The tag is the newest tag of the form vX.Y.Z with the branch's X.Y, by sort -V: v0.9.10 is newer than v0.9.9. Other tags, such as v0.9.11-rc1, are ignored.
  2. The tag must be an ancestor of HEAD.
  3. HEAD may differ from the tag only in these files: anything under the top-level docs/, mkdocs.yml, mkdocs.mike.yml. A docs/ folder anywhere else, such as src/docs/, does not count.

On success the guard prints the tag, which becomes the version's title. On failure it prints one of these messages on stderr, exits 1, and nothing is published:

Message Cause not a docs/X.Y branch: <ref> The first argument is not a docs/ branch. not a release tag vX.Y.Z or a docs/X.Y branch: <ref> The branch is docs/ but not docs/X.Y. docs/X.Y has no vX.Y.* release tag No release tag of that minor exists. <tag> is not a X.Y release The tag given as the second argument is of another minor. not a release tag: <tag> The second argument does not start with v. <tag> is not an ancestor of docs/X.Y The branch does not contain its newest release tag, for example after a patch release it has not moved to. docs/X.Y changes files outside docs/: <files>; code fixes need a release The branch changes other files than the docs. The files are listed, space-separated.

For example:

docs/0.2 changes files outside docs/: src/prometheus_exporter/app.uc; code fixes need a release

To run it locally, check out the branch, make sure the release tags are fetched, and pass the branch name:

devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh docs/0.2

docs.title: Links to the documentation
docs.text:
Where the link is It points to Always-current places: the README, the repository's homepage, forum posts <site_url>latest/... CHANGELOG.md <site_url>X.Y/..., the minor of the section the link is in Release notes <site_url>X.Y/..., the minor of the release Shipped files: everything under files/, src/ and luci/, and openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile (including URL:=) <site_url>X.Y/..., the package's current minor Pages of the documentation Relative paths, never the site's URL

site_url is the site's base URL without a version, set in mkdocs.yml, here https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/.

docs.title: Link check
docs.text:
make lint runs devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh, which checks every pinned link, <site_url><X.Y>/, in the shipped files and in CHANGELOG.md:

  • site_url is read from mkdocs.yml, with or without quotes; a missing trailing / is added. While site_url is unset, nothing is checked and the check passes.
  • In shipped files the minor must be the one of PKG_VERSION in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile: PKG_VERSION:=0.1.0 requires 0.1.
  • In CHANGELOG.md the minor must be the one of the enclosing ## [X.Y.Z] heading. Any other ## heading, such as ## [Unreleased], and the text before the first ## heading allow no pinned link at all. ### headings do not change the section.
  • Links to latest/ and links under other URLs are not checked.

CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog: ## [Unreleased] on top, then one ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD section per release, newest first. Only the ## [X.Y.Z] part of the heading is read.

A failure prints every wrong link and exits 1:

pinned docs links to the wrong version:
files/etc/config/prometheus-exporter:1: https://example.org/ucode-prometheus-exporter/0.9/ (expected 0.10)
CHANGELOG.md:5: https://example.org/ucode-prometheus-exporter/0.10/ (outside a release section)

docs.title: Files and scripts
docs.text: File Role .github/workflows/docs.yml The docs workflow: triggers, jobs. mkdocs.yml The site. Has no mike settings; make -C docs build and serve use it. mkdocs.mike.yml The versioned site: inherits mkdocs.yml and adds the search and mike plugins (canonical_version: latest, alias_type: copy), the version selector (extra.version.provider: mike) and the theme overrides in docs/overrides/. Used by build-mike and by the publish job. docs/overrides/main.html The outdated-version banner. devenv/gh-pages/404.html The 404 redirect, copied to the root of gh-pages on every publish. devenv/services/docs/Dockerfile The docs tools image, ucode-prometheus-exporter-docs: the mkdocs-material image plus requirements.txt, git, coreutils and Node. devenv/services/docs/requirements.txt Pinned mkdocs-material and mike, for the tools image and the publish job. devenv/scripts/docs-version.sh Maps a ref to its docs version. devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh The docs-only guard. devenv/scripts/docs-publish.sh Publishes one version. devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh The link check. test/docs/*_test.sh, test/docs/404_test.js Tests of the four scripts and of the 404 redirect, run by make -C docs test.

docs.title: docs-version.sh REF
docs.text:
Prints the version X.Y of a release tag vX.Y.Z or of a branch docs/X.Y. REF may carry a refs/tags/ or refs/heads/ prefix. Anything else prints not a release tag vX.Y.Z or a docs/X.Y branch: REF on stderr and exits 1.

$ devenv/scripts/docs-version.sh refs/tags/v0.10.2
0.10

docs.title: docs-guard.sh BRANCH [TAG]
docs.text: Checks HEAD as the tip of BRANCH, docs/X.Y with an optional refs/heads/ prefix, against TAG, by default the newest vX.Y.Z tag of that minor. See Docs-only guard. Prints the tag and exits 0, or prints a message on stderr and exits 1.

docs.title: docs-publish.sh REF
docs.text:
Publishes the current checkout as version X.Y of REF, a release tag or a docs/X.Y branch, with an optional refs/ prefix, to origin's gh-pages. Run from the repository root, with mike installed and a git committer configured.

  1. Maps REF to its version with docs-version.sh. For a docs/ branch, runs docs-guard.sh and takes the title from the tag it prints; for a tag, the title is the tag. The leading v is dropped.
  2. Fetches gh-pages from origin into the local gh-pages branch, if it exists there.
  3. Applies the latest rule: mike deploy -F mkdocs.mike.yml --title <title> --update-aliases X.Y latest and mike set-default -F mkdocs.mike.yml latest, or only mike deploy -F mkdocs.mike.yml --title <title> X.Y.
  4. Writes 404.html and .nojekyll to the root of gh-pages, in a separate commit, Root files: 404 redirect to latest, .nojekyll, only if they changed.
  5. Pushes gh-pages to origin.

It exits non-zero, before anything is pushed, if REF is not a release tag or a docs branch, or if the guard refuses.

docs.title: docs-links.sh [ROOT]
docs.text: Runs the link check on the repository at ROOT, by default the one the script is in. Exits 0 when every pinned link is right or site_url is unset, 1 otherwise.

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: A failure carries an uppercase code, from src/prometheus_exporter/errors.uc, and a detail. It is written CODE (detail), or CODE alone without one: in the log (collector '<name>': CODE (detail), see Log messages), in check, in the ubus object's replies and on LuCI's status page. A collector that fails has node_scrape_collector_success 0.

docs.title: Collectors and their sources
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by SOURCE_UNREADABLE A file the collector reads is not there or cannot be read. The detail names it. the collectors bmx7, conntrack, cpu, dhcp_leases, diskstats, entropy, filefd, filesystem, loadavg, meminfo, nat_traffic, netstat, snmp6, sockstat, softnet, timesync, uci_dhcp_host, uname, vmstat SOURCE_INVALID What the collector read is not what it expects: a file, a ubus reply or a program's output it cannot parse. The detail says where. services.uc; the collectors bmx7, chrony, conntrack, cpu, dawn, dhcp_leases, diskstats, dnsmasq, entropy, filefd, filesystem, hostapd_stations, loadavg, ltq-dsl, meminfo, modemmanager, mwan3, netclass, netdev, netstat, nft-counters, openwrt, openwrt_interfaces, qdisc, realtek-poe, selinux, sockstat, softnet, time, timesync, ubnt-manager, unbound, vmstat, wifi, wifi_stations, wireguard COLLECTOR_CRASHED The collector died with an exception. The detail is the exception's first line. scrape.uc COLLECTOR_NO_RESULT The collector returned something other than a Result. The detail says what. scrape.uc COLLECTOR_INVALID A collector module that cannot be loaded as one (its meta or collect), which the exporter leaves out; or a query that names a collector that is not installed, or one that is disabled, which is answered 400. loader.uc, scrape.uc

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by CONFIG_INVALID An option has a value the exporter does not take, or options that go together are not set together. The detail is <option>: expected <what>, got <value> (never the value of auth_password), or what is missing. auth.uc, config.uc; the collectors diskstats, vmstat FILE_UNWRITABLE The init script could not write or remove uhttpd's basic auth file, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf. auth.uc

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by NEED_MISSING A capability the collector needs is not installed: nl80211 without ucode-mod-nl80211, socket without ucode-mod-socket. deps.uc UBUS_CONNECT_FAILED The exporter could not connect to ubus. deps.uc UBUS_CALL_FAILED A ubus call failed. The detail is <object> <method>: <status>, as Not found. deps.uc, services.uc NL80211_FAILED An nl80211 request failed. The detail is the device and the kernel's error. deps.uc RTNL_FAILED An rtnetlink request failed. The detail is the kernel's error. deps.uc SOCKET_FAILED A Unix socket is missing, refused the connection, or sent no more of its reply in time. The detail names the socket. deps.uc COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED The collector ran a program its meta.commands does not list. deps.uc COMMAND_FAILED A program could not start or exited with a status other than 0. The detail is <program>: exit status <n> or <program>: cannot start. deps.uc COMMAND_TIMEOUT A program was still running when the collector's seconds for programs were spent, and was killed with every process it started; or the collector asked to run one after they were spent. deps.uc

docs.title: Exposition text
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by EXPOSITION_INVALID Text that is not valid Prometheus exposition format: a *.prom file of textfile, which the collector then leaves out. The detail names the line. exposition.uc

docs.title: Files and Packages
docs.text: Every package is architecture-independent (PKGARCH:=all), built from openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, version <PKG_VERSION>-r<PKG_RELEASE>. Each collector package, group package and the LuCI app depends on the base package of the very same version.

docs.title: ucode-prometheus-exporter
docs.text: The exporter, its service, its ubus object and the base collectors.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
uhttpd, uhttpd-mod-ucode, ucode, ucode-mod-fs, ucode-mod-ubus, ucode-mod-uci, ucode-mod-rtnl, ucode-mod-log, rpcd-mod-ucode (the ubus object), ucode-mod-uloop (its status without blocking rpcd), ucode-mod-zlib (gzip), ucode-mod-digest (basic auth's hashes).

It conflicts with prometheus-node-exporter-ucode and prometheus-node-exporter-lua: apk installs neither beside it, nor it beside either.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Path Content /etc/config/prometheus-exporter The configuration. A conffile: an upgrade keeps it when it was changed. See UCI configuration. /etc/init.d/prometheus-exporter The service. See Service commands. /etc/uci-defaults/prometheus-exporter-import Takes over a feed exporter's settings, once. See How to move from the feed's exporters. /etc/hotplug.d/ntp/90-prometheus-exporter Keeps busybox ntpd's last event for timesync. /usr/bin/prometheus-exporter The command. See The prometheus-exporter command. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/handler.uc uhttpd's handler for /metrics. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/check.uc service prometheus-exporter check, and with --config, the check of start and reload. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/status.uc What status prints of a running service. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/jail.uc The jail's mounts; --missing, the paths not there yet; --make, the directories the service makes. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/auth.uc Writes or removes basic auth's file. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/watch.uc The watch instance. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/import.uc The import the uci-defaults script runs. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/rpc-status.uc The scrape of the ubus object's status. /usr/share/rpcd/ucode/prometheus-exporter.uc rpcd's plugin: the ubus object. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter/*.uc The exporter's modules. version.uc holds the package's version. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter/collectors/<module>.uc The base collectors.

docs.text:
Path Content /var/run/prometheus-exporter/ Mode 0700. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf Basic auth's file, mode 0600, while basic auth is on. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/state/ The handler's state. See The jail. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/timesync/ntpd busybox ntpd's last event.

All are on tmpfs: none survives a reboot.

docs.title: Collector packages
docs.text: ucode-prometheus-exporter-<name>, one per collector not in the base package. Each installs /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter/collectors/<module>.uc and depends on the base package and on what its collector needs: see Collectors. Installing or removing one reloads an enabled service.

docs.title: Group packages
docs.text: ucode-prometheus-exporter-network, -wireless, -hardware and -full install no files: each depends on its collectors' packages. Removing a group from a device's world lets apk remove its collectors too. Which collectors each holds is in Collectors.

docs.title: luci-app-prometheus-exporter
docs.text: LuCI's pages for the exporter. Depends on luci-base and the base package. Its files are in LuCI app. Installing and removing it clears LuCI's caches and reloads rpcd.

docs.title: Source tree
docs.text: Path Content src/prometheus_exporter/ The modules, installed to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter/. src/prometheus_exporter/collectors/ The collectors. files/ What the base package installs besides the modules. luci/ The LuCI app. openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile The package Makefile. test/unit/ Unit tests; test/unit/prometheus_exporter/ mirrors src/prometheus_exporter/. test/integration/ Integration tests. test/fixtures/ What devices answered, for the tests. test/bench/ The benchmark. test/browser/ The LuCI app's Playwright tests. test/docs/ The documentation tooling's tests. devenv/ The development environment: Docker images and scripts. docs/ This documentation.

docs.title: HTTP Endpoint
docs.text: uhttpd serves the exporter's handler, /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/handler.uc, under the prefix /metrics, on port listen_port (9100) of the addresses of listen_interface (loopback), or of every address for *. With cert and key both set and both there it serves HTTPS, otherwise HTTP. See UCI configuration.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text: Request Answer /metrics, any method A scrape. A path under /metrics, such as /metrics/x The same scrape: uhttpd hands the handler every path with that prefix. Any other path 404, from uhttpd: its document root is /dev/null.

docs.title: Query string
docs.text:
Parameter Meaning collect[]=<name> Scrape this collector. Repeat it for several; they are scraped in the order given, once each. collect=<name> The same, as the feed's ucode exporter spelled it. exclude[]=<name> Leave this collector out.

A name is a collector's name (ltq-dsl) or its module (ltq_dsl), URL-encoded or not. Without collect[], a scrape runs every enabled collector, in the order of their names, less those excluded. Other parameters are ignored.

Query Status Body Names only installed, enabled collectors 200 OK The scrape. Names a collector that is not installed, in collect[] or exclude[] 400 Bad Request COLLECTOR_INVALID (unknown collector '<name>') Names a disabled collector in collect[] 400 Bad Request COLLECTOR_INVALID (collector '<name>' is disabled)

docs.title: The scrape
docs.text:
Content-Type: text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8: the Prometheus text exposition format, version 0.0.4.

  • Each collector's families, merged by name: a family two collectors write is written once, with the samples of both. A family declared with two types keeps the first, drops the later samples, and logs a warning.
  • Then, for every collector that ran: node_scrape_collector_duration_seconds, node_scrape_collector_success and node_scrape_collector_observing, labeled collector. Then ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version}. See Metrics.
  • A collector that fails keeps the samples it wrote before it failed. One with nothing to observe writes none.
  • With option omit_zero_values '1', samples of counters whose value is 0 are left out.

A collector's failure does not fail the scrape: the answer is still 200 OK.

docs.title: Compression
docs.text:
While option compress is 1 (the default):

  • Every reply has Vary: Accept-Encoding.
  • A 200 reply is gzip-compressed, with Content-Encoding: gzip, when the request's Accept-Encoding takes gzip: gzip or x-gzip with a q other than 0, or * with a q other than 0 when it names neither. gzip;q=0 refuses it.
  • zlib's level is 1, the fastest.

With option compress '0', no reply is compressed and none has Vary.

docs.title: Basic auth
docs.text:
With auth_user and auth_password set, the handler checks every request before it scrapes, against uhttpd's config file, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf:

Request Status Headers Body Over HTTP 403 Forbidden Basic auth takes HTTPS only. Without an Authorization: Basic header, or with a user or password that does not match 401 Unauthorized WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="prometheus-exporter" Unauthorized. With the user and password As without basic auth Any, when the file is there but is not one line of a user and a hash for /metrics 500 Internal Server Error Basic auth is not configured as it should be; see the log.

These replies are Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8. The init script never serves basic auth over HTTP: the 403 is for a request that reaches the handler without TLS all the same.

The handler reads the file, and compress, once, when uhttpd starts it. A change of either restarts uhttpd: see Service commands.

The password is checked against the hash: $1$ (MD5-crypt), $5$ (SHA-256-crypt) or $6$ (SHA-512-crypt), of at most 2000 rounds. After a request is let in, the handler keeps a digest of its Authorization header in its state, and lets in a later request with the same header on the digest alone. See The jail.

docs.title: Keep-alive
docs.text: uhttpd keeps an idle connection open http_keepalive seconds (70), with -k: Keep-Alive: timeout=70. At 0 it answers Connection: close and closes each connection once it has answered.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• How to serve HTTPS with basic auth
  • How to compress scrapes
  • About the security model

docs.title: The Jail
docs.text: uhttpd, and with it the exporter, runs in procd's jail (ujail), named prometheus-exporter, with no_new_privs. The jail holds what the exporter needs, what its installed and enabled collectors declare, and nothing else. src/prometheus_exporter/jail.uc works out the mounts; /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/jail.uc prints them for the init script.

docs.title: What every jail has
docs.text:
From What The jail's options procfs, sysfs, the ubus socket, /dev/log. The exporter /usr/lib/uhttpd_ucode.so, /lib/libubus.so*, /lib/libuci.so*, /usr/lib/libnl*.so*, /usr/lib/libz.so*, /usr/lib/ucode, /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter, /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/handler.uc. The configuration /etc/config/prometheus-exporter. HTTPS, with cert set cert, key, /lib/libustream-*.so*, /usr/lib/libustream-*.so*. Basic auth Its file, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf. The state /var/run/prometheus-exporter/state, read-write.

Every mount is read-only but the state.

docs.title: What a collector gets
docs.text:
For each installed collector that is enabled:

Declared in meta Mounted configs: [ 'dhcp' ] /etc/config/dhcp. exec in needs /bin/sh, which runs its programs. commands: [ 'nft' ] Each program, where PATH (/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin) finds it. ujail mounts its shared libraries along with it. optional_commands The same, where the program is installed; nothing, and no warning, where it is not. paths Each path: see below.

A disabled collector gets nothing. Nothing of /etc/config is there but the configs the enabled collectors name and the exporter's own. Which mounts each collector gets is in Collectors and in check.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
meta.paths lists what a collector reads outside procfs and sysfs:

Entry Mounted '/var/run/bmx7/json' That path. '{directory}' The value of the string option directory. { path: '{directory}', owned: true } That path, which is the exporter's own: the service makes it, with its parents (mode 0755), when it is not there. (options, uci) => [ ... ] What the function returns for the collector's options and the configs it reads.

A path is refused, with a warning, when it is not absolute, holds a space, a control or a glob character, is not plain (//, ., .., or a trailing /), or is one of the directories every service shares:

/, /bin, /dev, /etc, /etc/config, /lib, /proc, /run, /sbin, /sys, /tmp, /tmp/run, /usr, /usr/bin, /usr/lib, /usr/sbin, /usr/share, /var, /var/run.

ujail cannot mount a socket: a collector declares the socket's directory.

docs.title: Missing paths
docs.text:
A path that is not there when the service starts is left out of the mounts, and check warns of it. While one is missing, the service runs a second instance, watch, with the missing paths:

  1. Every 5 seconds it looks for them.
  2. Once one is there, it logs <path> is there now: reloading to mount it at info and sends procd the event prometheus-exporter.path.
  3. The event reloads the service, which mounts the path and restarts uhttpd with it. The reload ends the watch instance, or starts it again for the paths still missing.
  4. If procd does not take the event, it logs cannot send procd prometheus-exporter.path; trying again in 60s at warning.

A path the service owns is never missing: it makes it first.

docs.title: State
docs.text:
/var/run/prometheus-exporter/state is the one path the jail mounts read-write. It is on tmpfs, mode 0700, inside /var/run/prometheus-exporter, also 0700; jail.uc --make makes both when the service starts.

Owner A uhttpd instance: the handler names it when uhttpd loads it, before any request, by the pid and start time of that process. Files <pid>-<start time>.<name>, mode 0600, at most 4096 bytes each, written whole: to <file>.new, then renamed. Other instances' files Removed when the handler loads. Lifetime Until the instance stops: a restart starts without state, a reload that keeps the instance keeps it. Used for Basic auth's cache, <instance>.auth: one digest of the last Authorization header let in.

docs.title: Files the service writes
docs.text: Path Mode Written by Mounted /var/run/prometheus-exporter/ 0700 jail.uc --make, auth.uc No /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf 0600 auth.uc, at each start: one line, /metrics:<user>:<hash>; removed without basic auth Read-only, with basic auth /var/run/prometheus-exporter/state/ 0700 jail.uc --make Read-write /var/run/prometheus-exporter/timesync/ 0755 jail.uc --make (timesync's owned path), or the hotplug script Read-only /var/run/prometheus-exporter/timesync/ntpd 0644 /etc/hotplug.d/ntp/90-prometheus-exporter, on each event of busybox ntpd, outside the jail With its directory /var/prometheus/ (textfile's directory) 0755 jail.uc --make Read-only

docs.title: Restarts
docs.text: procd binds files into the jail. A file replaced by a new one, as uci commit replaces a config, stays the old one inside. So procd watches, for the uhttpd instance, the configs it mounts from /etc/config, every collector module and basic auth's file, and restarts the instance on reload when one changed.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Collector interface: what a collector declares.
  • About the security model

docs.title: Log Messages
docs.text:
The exporter logs to syslog as prometheus-exporter, facility daemon, each line at its own priority. Read it with logread -e prometheus-exporter.

Priority For err What stops it doing its job: an invalid configuration, a collector that does not load. warning What it does without: a collector that fails, which the scrape answers without; a path the jail cannot mount. info What it says of itself: how many collectors it serves, a directory it made, the settings it took over.

A collector with nothing to observe logs nothing. Neither the password of basic auth nor its hash is ever logged.

docs.title: The handler
docs.text:
Logged by uhttpd's handler, with the pid of the uhttpd process.

Message Priority When serving <n> collectors[, with basic auth][, gzip when asked] info uhttpd loaded the handler. cannot load collector '<module>': <error> err A collector module does not compile or import. It is left out. skipping collector: COLLECTOR_INVALID (<module>: <why>) err A module's meta or collect is not valid. It is left out. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf is not one line of a user and a hash for /metrics: every request is denied err Basic auth's file is there, and wrong. collector '<name>': <CODE (detail)> warning A collector failed in a scrape. See Error codes. collector '<name>': <message> warning A collector that succeeded said something with its log capability: textfile's skipped <file>: <why>. collector '<name>': '<family>' declared with two types; later samples dropped warning A collector declared a family twice. '<family>' declared with two types by different collectors; later samples dropped warning Two collectors declared a family with two types. main: <CODE (detail)> err A scrape read a main section it does not take, and used the defaults.

docs.title: The init script

docs.title: LuCI App
docs.text: luci-app-prometheus-exporter adds two pages to LuCI. It depends on luci-base and on the exporter's base package of the same release, and calls the ubus object the base package serves.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Menu Path View Services → Prometheus exporter admin/services/prometheus-exporter prometheus-exporter/settings Status → Prometheus exporter admin/status/prometheus-exporter prometheus-exporter/status

Both need the ACL luci-app-prometheus-exporter and the config prometheus-exporter.

docs.title: Services → Prometheus exporter
docs.text: The main section and the collector sections of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, in two tabs.

docs.title: Exporter tab
docs.text:
Field Option Notes Enable enabled Listen on listen_interface The interfaces of the ubus object's interfaces, and Every address (*). A saved interface netifd does not list is kept. Port listen_port Keep-alive http_keepalive TLS certificate cert TLS key key Basic auth user auth_user Basic auth password auth_password Never filled in. A password typed here is sent to hash_password on Save, and the hash it answers is saved. Empty, the saved hash stays. Compress compress Leave out zero values omit_zero_values Time for programs exec_timeout
  • Every field is written, at its default too (option enabled '1'), but for the TLS files and basic auth, which are left out while empty. Emptying another field is refused.
  • Emptying the user takes basic auth away, its hash with it.
  • Basic auth without both TLS files, and a user without a password, are refused.

docs.title: Collectors tab
docs.text:
One row per collector the ubus object's collectors lists: its title with its help below, its package (base or the package's name), a switch for enabled, and, for a collector with options, an Edit button. Collectors that are installed and do not load are listed above the form.

Edit opens a dialog with:

  • a field per option of the collector, by its type, with its help and datatype;
  • for a collector that runs programs, a field for the core's timeout, whose placeholder is the seconds it gets while it is empty: its own default, or exec_timeout as the Exporter tab has it;
  • read-only, the configs it reads and what the jail mounts for it.

The dialog's Save stages its values in uci, where they show among the unsaved changes; Dismiss drops them. The page's Save & Apply applies them with the rest.

A collector has a config collector section only while something differs from its defaults, its switch included. The section is added when a value first differs and removed once all are back. While it is there, it holds the switch and every option the collector declares, each written out; timeout only when it is set. A collector whose row did not change keeps its section as it was.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: Values are checked with the ubus object's validate, as the exporter reads them: the Exporter tab's while they are typed and again before Save, a dialog's while they are typed and again before it stages them. Nothing the exporter would refuse is saved or staged.

docs.title: Status → Prometheus exporter
docs.text:
Part Content Service Whether it is enabled in the settings, starts at boot and runs; where it serves /metrics, marked (reachable from the router only) on loopback; whether a scrape logs in, over HTTPS; whether it is compressed. Collectors Each collector's state, OK, Failed, Nothing to observe (with why) or Not run (disabled); its duration; its error; and what the jail mounts for it.

The scrape is the ubus object's status, run on the router outside the jail, when the page opens and on Refresh, never on a timer.

docs.title: Make Targets
docs.text: Every target runs in Docker; nothing is installed on the host. fixtures and bench-device reach a device over ssh.

docs.title: Tests and checks
docs.text: Target Description test The unit, integration and docs generator tests, with utest, in the OpenWrt image of OPENWRT_VERSION. unit test/unit/ only. integration test/integration/ only. watch All tests, then again whenever a file under src/, test/, files/, devenv/scripts/ or docs/gen/ changes. lint Loads every module on the release's ucode, so a function it lacks fails here; compiles every test, program and handler; sh -n every shell script; parses the JSON of luci/ and the LuCI views (as the function bodies LuCI compiles them into, with quickjs); fails on LuCI code that could turn data into markup (devenv/scripts/luci-dom-lint.sh); checks the pinned documentation links (devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh, see Link check); and fails while a generated reference page is not what docs-gen would write. Then checks that luci/po/templates/prometheus-exporter.pot is what pot would write. shell A shell in the development image. image Rebuilds the development image, pulling its base again.

docs.title: Packages and the device
docs.text: Target Description package Builds the apks with the OpenWrt SDK of OPENWRT_ARCH and OPENWRT_VERSION, into bin/. package-check package, then installs the packages offline in an OpenWrt image that carries their dependencies, scrapes a real uhttpd on loopback, calls the ubus object in a real rpcd, with the base package alone and then with the LuCI app, and checks the files, dependencies and ACL. e2e package, then boots OpenWrt (procd, ubusd, netifd) in a privileged container without network and checks the service in its jail as packages come and go and its config changes, and its ubus object, without LuCI. lab package, then OpenWrt under procd in a privileged container, left running, with every collector package and the LuCI app installed: LuCI on http://LAB_ADDRESS:LAB_LUCI_PORT/ (root, no password) and /metrics on http://LAB_ADDRESS:LAB_METRICS_PORT/metrics. make lab again starts it afresh with new packages. See How to use the lab. lab-down Removes the lab's container. browser package, then the Playwright tests of test/browser/ against LuCI in a container: the built packages, the ubus object in a real rpcd, real collectors, a stand-in for procd and netifd. Results and screenshots in bin/browser/. pot Writes luci/po/templates/prometheus-exporter.pot with openwrt/luci's scanner. Fails, and writes nothing, when the scanner warns. fixtures Reads the sources of test/fixtures/SOURCES from HOST over ssh into test/fixtures/NAME/. See How to capture fixtures.

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text: Target Description bench Each collector and whole scrapes on the generated worlds, in the package-check image: a table, and bin/bench/<label>.json. Checks the scaling and memory budgets of test/bench/budgets.uc, and, unconstrained, the time budgets too. bench-worlds Writes the worlds to bin/bench/worlds/. bench-device The benchmark on HOST over ssh, from its /tmp, with its own ucode; nothing is installed and everything copied is removed. bench-qemu package and bench-worlds, then the benchmark on OpenWrt's malta target in qemu-system-mipsel, a MIPS 24Kc, with the built packages installed from the release's feed. bench-src With BENCH_REV, extracts that revision's src/ into bin/bench/rev-<rev>. bench and bench-device run it.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Target Description docs make -C docs build. docs-mike make -C docs build-mike. docs-test make -C docs test. docs-serve make -C docs serve. docs-gen Writes the generated reference pages, docs/reference/collectors.md, metrics.md, uci-config.md and error-codes.md, from the code, the fixtures and docs/gen/notes.uc, in the development image. Fails, writing nothing, when the notes contradict the code. See How to write documentation.

test, unit, integration, watch, lint, shell and docs-gen run in the image ucode-prometheus-exporter-openwrt:<arch>-<version>-<hash>, built on first use from devenv/services/openwrt/Dockerfile; <hash> is the Dockerfile's, so worktrees with different Dockerfiles do not overwrite each other's image. docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The metric families each collector writes, and those a scrape writes of itself. Types, labels and help texts are what the collectors write: each collector runs as a scrape runs it, on each set of captures in test/fixtures/ (an access point, a router, a second router, made-up captures), with its defaults and with each boolean option the other way. A family that only an option writes says which.

The labels are those seen on the captures; a collector leaves out a label it has no value for, so a device may show fewer. Families whose names hold what the source reports (a driver's statistics, a kernel table's fields) are one row, their name a pattern in <>. Families no capture shows are listed from the collector's code, and say why.

Renamed metrics lists the names that changed from the feed's exporters.

docs.title: Service Commands
docs.text: The init script is /etc/init.d/prometheus-exporter (procd, START=60). Every action is also service prometheus-exporter <action>.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action What it does start Unless option enabled '0': checks the configuration (check.uc --config), sets up basic auth's file, makes the directories the collectors own and the state directory, and hands procd the uhttpd instance, in its jail. Refuses an invalid configuration, logging why at err. Waits for the listen interface: with no address on it yet, it logs deferring start until listen interface <interface> becomes ready and starts once the interface comes up. stop Stops the instances. restart stop, then start. The new instance starts without state. reload Checks the configuration. Invalid, it keeps the running instance and logs why; valid, it runs start again, and procd restarts the instance only if its command line, mounts or watched files changed. enable, disable Adds or removes the boot link /etc/rc.d/S60prometheus-exporter. enabled Exits 0 when the boot link is there. running Exits 0 when procd runs the service. status procd's state of the service, then one line: disabled (option enabled in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter), or, while it runs, where it listens. See status. check Checks the configuration, lists every installed collector and runs a scrape, outside the jail. See check.

option enabled in the main section and the boot link are separate: enabled '0' stops the service whether or not it is enabled at boot.

docs.text:
While the service runs:

running

One URL per address uhttpd listens on: http:// for HTTP, https:// for HTTPS, *:<port> for every address. nothing when it listens on none. , basic auth uhttpd has basic auth's file: a scrape logs in. , gzip when asked option compress is on. , serving <n> collectors The installed collectors that are enabled.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
service prometheus-exporter check runs /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/check.uc. It prints a line per finding, then every installed collector, then the jail's mounts:

ok   main: HTTP on every address, port 9100, keepalive 70s, exec_timeout 5s, gzip when asked
ok   collectors: 17 installed collectors, their options valid
ok   scrape, outside the jail: 17 of 17 collectors succeeded, 1 with nothing to observe
ok   scrape: wifi has nothing to observe: no wireless radios

collectors: 17 installed, 17 enabled
  conntrack (Connection tracking): section 'conntrack', enabled
      needs    fs
  ...
  textfile (Text files): section 'textfile', enabled
      option   directory="/var/prometheus" # The directory of the *.prom files.
      needs    fs log
      paths    /var/prometheus
      makes    /var/prometheus
      mounts   /var/prometheus
  ...

jail mounts:
  /bin/sh
  /etc/config/prometheus-exporter
  /var/prometheus
  /var/run/prometheus-exporter/timesync

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Each finding starts with ok, warn or FAIL. Only a FAIL makes check exit 1; it exits 0 otherwise.

Finding Level main: <listen summary>, exec_timeout <n>s, gzip when asked (or no compression (option compress)) ok main: <CODE (detail)>: an option of the main section the exporter does not take, or options that go together not set together FAIL main: cert and key go together; with only cert, it serves HTTP warn main: <file> is missing; it serves HTTP until it is there warn main: <file> is missing; basic auth takes HTTPS only, so the service does not start until it is there FAIL collectors: <n> installed collectors, their options valid ok collector <name>, section '<module>': <CODE (detail)>: an option of its section it does not take FAIL section '<name>' names no installed collector; it is ignored warn an unnamed collector section is ignored: name it after its collector's module warn cannot load collector '<module>': ... or skipping collector: COLLECTOR_INVALID (...): a module the loader left out warn jail: <collector>: <problem>: a path or command the jail cannot give warn jail: <collector>: <path> is not there; the service mounts it once it is warn scrape, outside the jail: <n> of <m> collectors succeeded[, <k> with nothing to observe] ok, or warn when one failed scrape: <collector>: <CODE (detail)>: a collector that failed warn scrape: <collector> has nothing to observe: <reason> ok

The listen summary is HTTP or HTTPS, on interface <name> or on every address, the port and the keepalive, and basic auth as user "<user>" when basic auth is on. The password's hash is never shown.

docs.title: Collectors
docs.text:
One block per installed collector, enabled or not:

Line Content <name> (<title>): section '<module>', enabled Its name, title, the section that configures it, and whether it is enabled. option Each of its own options: <name>=<value> # <help>. timeout For a collector that runs programs: its seconds, and where they come from: its section's option timeout, the collector's own (meta.timeout) or the main section's exec_timeout. needs, configs Its meta.needs and meta.configs. paths, makes The paths it reads outside procfs and sysfs, and those the service makes for it. commands Each program it runs, <name>=<path>, or (not found). mounts What the jail mounts for it, when it is enabled.

The scrape check runs is outside the jail, as root, with the committed configuration. A collector that works in check and fails under procd lacks something in the jail: see The jail.

docs.title: procd
docs.text:
Instance Command When instance1 /usr/sbin/uhttpd -f -c <auth file or /dev/null> -h /dev/null -S -D -o /metrics -O /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/handler.uc [-r prometheus-exporter] -k <keepalive> [-C <cert> -K <key>] -p\|-s <address>:<port> ... While the service is enabled. -s (HTTPS) with cert and key both set and both there, -p (HTTP) otherwise. One -p or -s per address of the listen interface, IPv4 and IPv6, or the port alone for *. -r only with basic auth. watch /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/watch.uc <path>... While a path an enabled collector reads is not there. See The jail.

Both are respawned by procd. The uhttpd instance runs in a jail: see The jail.

docs.text: Trigger Action A change of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, or of a config an enabled collector reads (meta.configs), applied by reload_config reload The listen interface going up or down, unless listen_interface is * reload The event prometheus-exporter.path, which the watch instance sends reload A change of a file procd watches for the instance: the configs it mounts, every collector module, basic auth's file procd restarts the instance on reload

docs.text:
Package On install On removal ucode-prometheus-exporter OpenWrt's defaults (run the uci-defaults script, enable and start the service), then reload rpcd; on an upgrade, restart a running service. Reload rpcd. A collector package reload an enabled service, which restarts it with the collector. A failed reload fails no install. docs.title: ubus Object
docs.text:
The ubus object prometheus-exporter belongs to the base package. rpcd serves it, from the ucode plugin /usr/share/rpcd/ucode/prometheus-exporter.uc, over src/prometheus_exporter/rpc.uc, whether or not the service runs. rpcd loads it when it starts or reloads; the package reloads rpcd when it is installed, upgraded or removed.

The object reads with the exporter's own modules and writes nothing. Each call reads the committed configuration and the installed collectors afresh.

$ ubus -v list prometheus-exporter
'prometheus-exporter' @085bb3ca
    "collectors":{}
    "validate":{"main":"Table","collectors":"Table"}
    "status":{}
    "interfaces":{}
    "hash_password":{"password":"String"}

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Arguments Reply collectors none { collectors: [ collector ], skipped: [ message ] } validate { main?, collectors? } { ok, errors: { main: { <option>: message }, collectors: { <module>: { <option>: message } } } } status none { service: { enabled, boot, running, error, auth, compress }, listen: [ url ], collectors: [ result ] } interfaces none { interfaces: [ { name, proto } ] } hash_password { password } { hash }

A call with malformed arguments, and one that fails, is answered { error, message }. See Errors.

docs.title: collectors
docs.text:
Every installed collector, in the order of their names, and the messages of the modules the loader left out (skipped).

Field of a collector Type Content name string Its name, as collect[] takes it. id string Its module: the name of its section. title, help string meta.title and meta.help. enabled boolean Whether its section enables it. package string or null The package that installed it, from apk's file lists; null when none did. base boolean or null Whether that is the base package. options array Its own options, in the order it declares them, then, for a collector that runs programs, the core's timeout. needs, configs, commands array meta.needs, meta.configs, meta.commands. jail object What the jail gives it: paths, owned, commands ({ <name>: <path or null> }), mounts, problems, missing. See The jail. error string or null The first option of its section the exporter does not take, as CODE (detail). Field of an option Type Content name string The option's name. core boolean true for the core's timeout, false for the collector's own. type string bool, int or string: the type of its default. default any Its default. For timeout, the seconds it gets while unset. default_from string timeout only: meta.timeout or exec_timeout, whose seconds the default is. help string or null What it does. datatype string or null See UCI configuration. value any Its value as the exporter reads it; as uci holds it when the exporter does not take it. set boolean Whether its section sets it. error string or null What the exporter expected of a value it does not take.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Checks values as the exporter would read them, without saving anything. main holds options of the main section and collectors options of collector sections, by module: values as uci holds them, as strings.

$ ubus call prometheus-exporter validate '{"main":{"listen_port":"0","auth_user":"p"}}'
{
    "ok": false,
    "errors": {
        "main": {
            "listen_port": "expected an integer from 1 to 65535, got 0",
            "auth_password": "basic auth needs the hash of a password along with auth_user",
            "auth_user": "basic auth needs HTTPS: set cert and key, or the password crosses the network in the clear"
        },
        "collectors": {

        }
    }
}
  • Each value is checked alone. An empty value is unset, and takes the default.
  • Options nobody declared, and collectors that are not installed, are ignored, as the exporter ignores them.
  • The main section's options that go together, basic auth's user and hash and the cert and key they need, are checked as if the values given were the whole section.
  • A collector section takes enabled, timeout for a collector that runs programs, and the collector's own options.
  • No message holds the value of auth_password.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Runs one scrape of the enabled collectors, outside the jail, and replies when it is done. rpcd runs it in a process of its own, /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/rpc-status.uc, and answers other calls meanwhile, the collectors' calls to objects rpcd serves (wireguard, luci) among them.

Field Type Content service.enabled boolean or null option enabled of the main section; null when that section is not valid. service.boot boolean Whether the boot link /etc/rc.d/S*prometheus-exporter is there. service.running boolean or null Whether procd runs the uhttpd instance; null when procd cannot be asked. service.error string or null Why procd could not be asked. service.auth boolean or null Whether basic auth is configured. service.compress boolean or null option compress. listen array The URLs the running instance listens on, as http://*:9100/metrics. collectors array One result per installed collector, in the order of their names. Field of a result Type Content name, id, title string As in collectors. enabled boolean Whether it ran: a disabled collector does not. success boolean or null Whether it succeeded; null when it did not run. observing boolean or null false for a collector with nothing to observe, true for any other that ran, null when it did not run. reason string or null Why it has nothing to observe, as dnsmasq is disabled. duration number or null Its seconds. error string or null Why it failed, as CODE (detail). mounts array What the jail mounts for it; empty when it is disabled.

docs.title: interfaces
docs.text:
The logical interfaces netifd has, in its order, as network.interface dump gives them: name and proto (null when it has none). It never reads /etc/config/network.

$ ubus call prometheus-exporter interfaces
{
    "interfaces": [
        {
            "name": "lan",
            "proto": "static"
        },
        {
            "name": "loopback",
            "proto": "static"
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: hash_password
docs.text:
A SHA-512-crypt hash of password, of 1000 rounds and a fresh salt of 16 characters, for auth_password:

$ ubus call prometheus-exporter hash_password '{"password":"…"}'
{
    "hash": "$6$rounds=1000$…"
}

The password is 1 to 256 bytes, without control characters. rpcd runs the method, unjailed, and logs neither the password nor the hash.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
error message When ARGS_INVALID main and collectors must be objects, collectors.<module> must be an object validate was given something else. ARGS_INVALID password: expected a password, password: expected a password of at most 256 bytes, password: expected a password without control characters hash_password was given a password it does not take. STATUS_FAILED cannot run /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/rpc-status.uc 2>/dev/null, ... printed no reply status could not run its scrape, or the scrape printed no reply. A code CODE (detail) interfaces could not ask netifd; hash_password had no random bytes.

ubus itself refuses arguments of the wrong type, as a string for main, with Invalid argument.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Over HTTP, through uhttpd-mod-ubus, a session needs the methods in its ACL. The LuCI app's ACL, luci-app-prometheus-exporter, grants collectors, interfaces, status and validate to read, and hash_password to write. See LuCI app.

docs.title: UCI Configuration
docs.text: The exporter's configuration is /etc/config/prometheus-exporter. The file is optional: every option has a default, an unset option takes it, and an option the exporter does not know is ignored. Changes apply on reload_config or service prometheus-exporter reload.

docs.title: The main section
docs.text:
config prometheus-exporter 'main'. The init script reads the first options, to start uhttpd; the exporter reads the others in each scrape.

Option Type Default Datatype Description Read by enabled boolean 1 — Run the service; 0 stops it. init script listen_interface string loopback — The logical interface uhttpd listens on, or * for every address. init script listen_port integer 9100 range(1,65535) The port uhttpd listens on. init script http_keepalive integer 70 uinteger Seconds an idle connection is kept open; 0 for none. init script cert string unset — The certificate to serve HTTPS with, along with key. init script key string unset — The private key of cert. init script auth_user string unset username The user a scrape logs in as (basic auth), with auth_password; HTTPS only. init script auth_password string unset crypt The crypt hash of the password of auth_user: $1$ (uhttpd -m), $5$ or $6$, as the ubus object's hash_password makes it. init script omit_zero_values boolean 0 — Leave out counters that are 0, most of which never move on a router. exporter compress boolean 1 — Send a scrape gzip-compressed when the scraper asks for it (Accept-Encoding: gzip); 0 never does. exporter exec_timeout integer 5 range(1,30) Seconds the programs a collector runs get in all in each scrape, unless the collector says otherwise; one still running then is killed. exporter

Options that go together, checked wherever the configuration is checked (start, reload, check, the ubus object's validate and LuCI):

  • auth_user without auth_password: basic auth needs the hash of a password along with auth_user.
  • auth_password without auth_user: basic auth needs a user along with auth_password.
  • Either without cert and key: basic auth needs HTTPS: set cert and key, or the password crosses the network in the clear.

docs.title: Collector sections
docs.text:
config collector '<module>', one per collector, named after its module: the collector's name with _ for - (ltq_dsl for ltq-dsl), as a uci section name cannot hold -. A collector without a section runs with its defaults. A section that names no installed collector, and one without a name, is ignored (check warns of both). Besides its own options, listed in Collectors, every collector has these:

Option Type Default Datatype Description enabled boolean 1 — Serve this collector; 0 leaves it out, and naming it in a query is a 400. timeout integer the collector's meta.timeout, else exec_timeout (5) range(1,30) Seconds the programs of this collector get in all in each scrape; one still running then is killed.

timeout is only for a collector that runs programs (exec in its needs); the others ignore it. No collector may declare an option named enabled, timeout.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
A boolean takes 1, yes, on, true, enabled for true and 0, no, off, false, disabled for false. An integer is decimal digits, with an optional -. A string is a single value, not a list. A datatype narrows what an option takes, by the name LuCI gives it; the exporter checks it itself:

Datatype Takes crypt a crypt hash: $1$ (uhttpd -m), $5$ or $6$ directory an absolute path file an absolute path range(1,30) an integer from 1 to 30 range(1,65535) an integer from 1 to 65535 regex a regular expression uinteger an integer of 0 or more username a user of 1 to 64 characters, without ":", spaces or control characters

directory and file check the path's form, not that it exists. A value an option does not take is CONFIG_INVALID: in the main section it stops start and reload, and in a collector's section that collector fails in each scrape. See Error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
config prometheus-exporter 'main'
    option enabled '1'
    option listen_interface 'loopback'
    option listen_port '9100'
    option http_keepalive '70'
    option omit_zero_values '0'
    option compress '1'
    option exec_timeout '5'

config collector 'textfile'
    option enabled '1'
    option directory '/var/prometheus'

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Lessons to follow from start to end, by doing. Each starts from nothing and ends with something working.

Tutorial You will Monitor a router with Prometheus Install the exporter on an OpenWrt router, open it to the LAN, scrape it with Prometheus and graph the router. Write your first collector Write, run, test and package a collector, and see it served by OpenWrt in the lab. For developers.

docs.title: Write Your First Collector
docs.text:
In this tutorial we will write a collector, tasks, that counts the tasks the kernel has, from /proc/loadavg. We will run it on the command line, test it, package it, and see it served by OpenWrt in the lab, in LuCI and at /metrics. Along the way we will meet the development environment: make shell, make test, test/context.uc, make docs-gen and make lab.

It takes about half an hour, most of it waiting for builds. At the end we will remove what we made: this collector is practice.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A checkout of the repository, and a terminal in it.
  • Docker, and make. Everything else runs in containers.
  • About 3 GB of disk for the images, the first time.

docs.title: 1. Run the tests
docs.text:
First, make sure everything works before we change anything:

make test

The first run builds the development image, OpenWrt's own, which takes a minute or two. Then the tests run, and the last lines say how they went:

Summary:

  1146 successes / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped / 0 ignored (49301 ms)

Your numbers will differ. What matters is 0 failures.

docs.title: 2. Look at the source
docs.text:
Our collector will read the fourth field of /proc/loadavg. Let's see it, in the development image:

make shell

cat /proc/loadavg

0.72 0.61 0.97 2/3199 81234

The fourth field, 2/3199, is the tasks that are runnable now and the tasks that exist. Leave the shell with exit.

docs.title: 3. Write the collector
docs.text:
Create src/prometheus_exporter/collectors/tasks.uc:

'use strict';

import * as Result from 'prometheus_exporter.result';
import * as errors from 'prometheus_exporter.errors';
import { first_line, fields } from 'prometheus_exporter.proc';

export const meta = {
    name: 'tasks',
    title: 'Scheduler tasks',
    help: 'Runnable and existing tasks, from /proc/loadavg.',
    needs: [ 'fs' ],
};

export function collect(deps, out) {
    let line = first_line(deps.fs, '/proc/loadavg');

    if (line == null)
        return Result.err(errors.SOURCE_UNREADABLE, '/proc/loadavg');

    let counts = split(fields(line)[3] ?? '', '/');

    if (length(counts) != 2)
        return Result.err(errors.SOURCE_INVALID, `/proc/loadavg: ${line}`);

    out.gauge('node_tasks_runnable', 'Tasks that are runnable now.')(null, counts[0]);
    out.gauge('node_tasks', 'Tasks that exist now.')(null, counts[1]);

    return Result.ok();
};

Notice three things. meta.needs asks for fs, and collect reads the file through deps.fs, not by importing fs: a collector only gets what it asks for. out.gauge declares a family and returns a function that records a sample. And collect returns a Result: Result.ok() when it worked, Result.err() with a code when it did not.

docs.title: 4. Run it
docs.text:
Back in the development image:

make shell

ucode -L /exporter/src files/usr/bin/prometheus-exporter -d src/prometheus_exporter/collectors tasks

This is the exporter's own command, run from the source tree, with the collectors of src/ and only ours. It prints a scrape:

# HELP node_tasks_runnable Tasks that are runnable now.
# TYPE node_tasks_runnable gauge
node_tasks_runnable 2
# HELP node_tasks Tasks that exist now.
# TYPE node_tasks gauge
node_tasks 3199
# HELP node_scrape_collector_duration_seconds node_exporter: Duration of a collector scrape.
...
node_scrape_collector_success{collector="tasks"} 1
...
ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version="dev"} 1

Our two families come first, then what every scrape says of each collector that ran: ours succeeded. The version is dev, as it is from a source tree. exit the shell.

docs.title: 5. Test it
docs.text:
Tests run the collector the way a scrape does, with fakes in place of the system: test/context.uc gives them. Create test/unit/prometheus_exporter/collectors/tasks_test.uc:

'use strict';

import { describe, it, assert } from 'utest';
import { with_collector } from 'context';
import * as tasks from 'prometheus_exporter.collectors.tasks';

describe('collectors.tasks', () => {
    it('counts the runnable and the existing tasks', () => {
        with_collector(tasks, { fs: { data: { '/proc/loadavg': '0.08 0.03 0.00 2/131 4567\n' } } }, (r) => {
            assert.match(true, r.result.ok);
            assert.match([
                '# HELP node_tasks_runnable Tasks that are runnable now.',
                '# TYPE node_tasks_runnable gauge',
                'node_tasks_runnable 2',
                '# HELP node_tasks Tasks that exist now.',
                '# TYPE node_tasks gauge',
                'node_tasks 131',
            ], r.lines);
        });
    });

    it('fails with SOURCE_UNREADABLE when /proc/loadavg cannot be read', () => {
        with_collector(tasks, { fs: { data: { '/proc/loadavg': null } } }, (r) => {
            assert.match('SOURCE_UNREADABLE', r.result.error);
            assert.match([ "collector 'tasks': SOURCE_UNREADABLE (/proc/loadavg)" ], r.logs);
        });
    });
});

with_collector hands the collector an fs that answers from data, runs it, and gives us what it wrote: r.result, r.lines, and r.logs, what the scrape would log. The second test hands it a file that cannot be read. Run only these:

make unit MODULES=test/unit/prometheus_exporter/collectors/tasks_test.uc

  2 successes / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped / 0 ignored (90 ms)

docs.title: 6. Package it
docs.text:
Now the whole suite:

make test

It fails, as it should. Among its output:

    ■ docs_gen.main.run > finds the notes and the code in agreement
        Expected 0 elements, got 1
...
    ■ collectors > tasks > is in the generated reference
        run make docs-gen: docs/reference/collectors.md has no tasks
    ■ collectors > tasks > is packaged once: in the base package or as its own, named after it
        tasks: base false, subpackage null

test/integration/collectors_test.uc holds every collector to what the repository owes it, and the documentation's generator finds a collector in no package. Ours has no package yet. Open openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, find the Collector lines, and add ours after sockstat's:

$(eval $(call Collector,tasks,tasks,scheduler tasks,))

That makes a package, ucode-prometheus-exporter-tasks. Then write the reference pages again, which the code decides:

make docs-gen

wrote docs/reference/collectors.md
wrote docs/reference/error-codes.md
wrote docs/reference/metrics.md

Open docs/reference/metrics.md and find the section of tasks: our two families are there, with their type and help, as the collector wrote them when the generator ran it on the captures of real routers in test/fixtures/. Now:

make test

The summary says 0 failures again.

docs.title: 7. See it on OpenWrt
docs.text:
The lab is OpenWrt under procd, in a container, with every package installed:

make lab

It builds the packages with OpenWrt's SDK, which takes a few minutes the first time, boots OpenWrt and installs them. It ends with:

The lab runs, as container ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab:
  LuCI      http://127.0.0.1:8080/  (root, no password)
  /metrics  http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics
  a shell   docker exec -it ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab ash
  stop it   make lab-down

Ask it for our collector:

curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics?collect[]=tasks' | grep '^node_tasks'

node_tasks_runnable 2
node_tasks 3255

Counted by our collector, in the exporter's jail, under procd. The numbers are your computer's: a container shares its host's kernel, and so its /proc/loadavg. Now open http://127.0.0.1:8080/, log in as root with no password, and go to Services → Prometheus exporter, tab Collectors: there is a row Scheduler tasks, with our help text and its package, ucode-prometheus-exporter-tasks. On Status → Prometheus exporter it is OK.

docs.title: 8. Clean up
docs.text:
Stop the lab:

make lab-down

and remove what we made, as this collector was practice:

rm src/prometheus_exporter/collectors/tasks.uc test/unit/prometheus_exporter/collectors/tasks_test.uc
git checkout openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile
make docs-gen

docs.title: What we did
docs.text: We wrote a collector that asks for one capability and writes two families, ran it on the command line, tested it with test/context.uc's fakes, gave it a package, generated its reference, and saw it served by OpenWrt in its jail and listed in LuCI.

docs.title: Monitor a Router with Prometheus
docs.text:
In this tutorial we will install the exporter on an OpenWrt router, look at its metrics on the router itself, open it to the LAN, and have a Prometheus on our computer scrape it and graph the router's load and traffic. Along the way we will meet the service's status and check, which tell us what the exporter does.

It takes about twenty minutes.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A router on OpenWrt 25.12, at 192.168.1.1 on its LAN, with internet access, and a shell on it: ssh root@192.168.1.1.

  • The exporter's base package, ucode-prometheus-exporter-0.1.0-r1.apk, copied to the router's /tmp:

    scp -O ucode-prometheus-exporter-0.1.0-r1.apk root@192.168.1.1:/tmp/

  • A computer on the router's LAN, with Docker.

If your router's address is not 192.168.1.1, use yours wherever it appears.

docs.title: 1. Install the exporter
docs.text:
On the router, install the package. apk fetches what it depends on from OpenWrt's feeds:

apk update
apk add --allow-untrusted /tmp/ucode-prometheus-exporter-0.1.0-r1.apk

apk lists what it installs, and ends with OK. The service starts on its own. Let's ask it how it is:

service prometheus-exporter status

running
listening on http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics, gzip when asked, serving 15 collectors

Notice where it listens: 127.0.0.1, the router's loopback. For now only the router itself can reach it.

docs.title: 2. Look at the metrics
docs.text:
Still on the router, ask for a scrape, as Prometheus will:

wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | grep '^node_load'

node_load1 0.08
node_load5 0.03
node_load15 0

These are the router's load averages. Now the last lines of the scrape:

wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | tail -n 4

node_scrape_collector_observing{collector="vmstat"} 1
# HELP ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info A metric with a constant '1' value labeled by the version of ucode-prometheus-exporter.
# TYPE ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info gauge
ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version="0.1.0-r1"} 1

Every scrape ends with what it says of itself: how long each collector took, whether it succeeded, and the exporter's version.

docs.title: 3. Open it to the LAN
docs.text:
Our computer is on the LAN, so we have the exporter listen there:

uci set prometheus-exporter.main.listen_interface=lan
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload
service prometheus-exporter status

running
listening on http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics, gzip when asked, serving 15 collectors

The address is now the router's LAN address. From the computer, check that it answers:

curl -s http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics | grep '^node_load1'

node_load1 0.08

docs.title: 4. Scrape it with Prometheus
docs.text:
On the computer, make a directory for Prometheus, and in it a file prometheus.yml:

global:
  scrape_interval: 15s

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: openwrt
    static_configs:
      - targets: [ '192.168.1.1:9100' ]

Start Prometheus in Docker, with that file:

docker run --rm -d --name prometheus -p 9090:9090 \
    -v "$PWD/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro" prom/prometheus

Open http://localhost:9090/targets. After a few seconds the openwrt job's target, http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics, is UP. If it says DOWN with connection refused, the exporter is still on loopback: go back to step 3.

docs.title: 5. Graph the router
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:9090/query, type this expression, and press Execute:

node_load1

One series, the router's one-minute load. Switch to the Graph tab to see it over time.

Now the traffic the router receives, in bytes per second, for each network device:

rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total[1m])

There is a series per device, labeled device. Give it a few minutes: rate needs several scrapes.

Last, ask which version runs there:

ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info

ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{instance="192.168.1.1:9100", job="openwrt", version="0.1.0-r1"}  1

docs.title: 6. Ask the exporter how it is doing
docs.text:
Back on the router:

service prometheus-exporter check

The first lines are its findings, something like:

ok   main: HTTP on interface lan, port 9100, keepalive 70s, exec_timeout 5s, gzip when asked
ok   collectors: 15 installed collectors, their options valid
ok   scrape, outside the jail: 15 of 15 collectors succeeded

Then one block per collector, with what it reads and what the service's jail gives it, and last, everything the jail mounts. Each ok is a check that passed; a problem would be a warn or FAIL line saying what is wrong.

Let's watch a collector go. Switch off softnet, the network softirq statistics:

uci set prometheus-exporter.softnet=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.softnet.enabled=0
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload
service prometheus-exporter status

running
listening on http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics, gzip when asked, serving 14 collectors

One collector fewer. In Prometheus, node_softnet_processed_total stops getting new samples. Switch it back on:

uci delete prometheus-exporter.softnet
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

docs.title: 7. Clean up
docs.text:
Stop Prometheus on the computer:

docker stop prometheus

The exporter keeps running on the router, on the LAN.

docs.title: What we did
docs.text: We installed the exporter, read a scrape on the router, opened it to the LAN, had Prometheus scrape it, and graphed the router's load and traffic. We asked the service for its status and its check, and saw it serve one collector fewer and then again.
